title: 第三章　作为绕道的资本主义

zh: 第三章　作为绕道的资本主义
en: 3 Capitalism as a Detour

zh: 在新冠疫情的众多受害者中，有一个不太引人注意的意外伤亡。2020 年的大封锁把世界推入大萧条以来最严重的经济衰退。数百万人因新冠病毒丧生，与此同时，更广泛的人失去了生计和经济前途。然而，在这场苦难之中，世界各地的股市在经历一次急剧下挫后，却经历了非凡增长的一年。股市的扩张紧随主要央行决定创造数万亿美元的新资产、几乎使资产负债表规模翻倍之后；它们使用的是被称为量化宽松的创造货币的方法，这种方法最早在应对 2008 年全球金融危机时被广泛部署。
银行资产的倍增拯救了金融市场。而伤亡的，是任何仍然认为我们的常识或经济学教科书懂得货币如何运作的残留信念。
en: Among the many victims of the Covid-19 pandemic, there was a minor, unexpected casualty. The Great Lockdown of 2020 pushed the world into the worst economic recession since the Great Depression. The loss of millions of lives to the coronavirus was accompanied by an even wider loss of livelihoods and economic futures. Yet, amid this hardship, stock markets around the world, after a sharp setback, experienced a year of extraordinary growth. Their expansion followed the decision of leading central banks to create trillions of dollars of new assets, almost doubling the size of their balance sheets, using the method of manufacturing money known as quantitative easing, first widely deployed in response to the global financial crisis of 2008.
The multiplying of banking assets saved the financial markets. The casualty was any lingering claim that our common sense, or the textbooks of economics, understood how money works.

zh: 为什么理解货币如此困难？这种困难又告诉了我们什么关于资本主义的事情？商业银行、利率、股票和债券交易、衍生品合约、量化宽松，以及创造信用和债务的各种机制的其他部分，似乎都处于我们日常理解和经济生活标准模型之外。
为什么金融业——它不知怎地制造了所有这些货币——比其他制造业分支更不透明？金融业更技术化、更抽象吗？货币工具的设计和生产，肯定不可能比微处理器或新冠疫苗的制造更复杂吧？答案不在于货币作为一个过程的
复杂性，而在于这个过程与我们用来理解它的观念之间的关系。
en: Why is it so hard to make sense of money? And what does this difficulty tell us about capitalism? The apparatus of commercial banking, interest rates, equity and bond trading, derivative contracts, quantitative easing, and other parts of the various mechanisms that create credit and debt seem to lie outside both our everyday comprehension and standard models of economic life.

Why is the industry of finance, which somehow manufactures all this money, rendered so much more opaque than other branches of manufacturing? Is the financial industry more technical, or more abstract? Surely the design and production of monetary instruments cannot be more complex than the making of a microprocessor, say, or a Covid-19 vaccine? The answer lies not in the
complexity of money as a process, but in the relation between the process and the ideas with which we make sense of it.

zh: 理解货币的困难，源于它的制造方式塑造了解释它的科学。像货币本身一样，经济学这门学科通过把其生产装置的大部分置于视野之外来运作。经济学是一种知识形式，它也像货币一样，通过假定一个极其简单的区分来运作：对象与其价格之间的差别，物质与货币之间的差别，金融与社会之间的差别，真实世界与其表象之间的差别。
这些问题不仅关乎理解货币。资本的托词正是通过这些看似自明的区分生产出来的。它们背后是我们对现代生活形式如何产生、如今又如何被治理的理解。要处理这些问题，除其他事项外，需要考察殖民和奴役在创造现代货币体系中的位置；所谓工业革命中进入制造业和雇佣劳动的
，这次绕道使货币显得仅仅是支付手段或价值的代表；以及十九世纪后期现代公司和现代银行作为新的货币创造机器的兴起。那些十九世纪后期的安排，部分正是在上一章埃及所探讨的那类帝国计划中出现的。这类计划既促成又掩盖了货币的制造，以及世界似乎被划分为金融与实体、虚构与物质——以及殖民者与被殖民者——这一更广泛效果的产生。
en: The difficulty in understanding money arises from the way its manufacturing has shaped the science that explains it. Like money itself, the discipline of economics works by placing out of sight much of the apparatus of its production. Economics is a form of knowledge that operates, again like money, by assuming a remarkably simple distinction: the difference between an object and its price, between the material and the monetary, between finance and society, and between the real world and its representation.

These issues concern not just making sense of money. The alibi of capital is produced through these apparently self-evident distinctions. Behind them lies our understanding of how modern forms of life came into being, and how they are governed today. Addressing them requires, among other things, considering the place of colonisation and enslavement in creating modern systems of money, the

into manufacturing and wage labour in the so-called industrial revolution that made money appear to be merely a means of payment or representation of value, and then the rise of the modern corporation and the modern bank in the later nineteenth century as new machines of money creation. Those late-nineteenth-century arrangements emerged in part in the kinds of imperial schemes explored in Egypt in the previous chapter. Such schemes facilitated and disguised both the making of money and the creating of the wider effect of a world that seemed divided into the financial and the real, the fictitious and the material – and the colonising and the colonised.

zh: 货币不是实物
en: Money Is No Object

zh: 什么是货币？直到最近，答案似乎显而易见。我们把它视为一种物品，形状是纸币和硬币，是它在手中呈现的日常样貌。我们主要把它的生产与现代国家的权力联系起来，因为政府授权铸造和印刷货币，并确立缴税和其他债务必须使用的法定货币。经济学家传统上用三种功能来定义它的用途。它是交换媒介，使人们能够在不诉诸物物交换的情况下交易商品和服务；它是记账单位，使企业能够记录商品价格并计算利润；它还是储存财富的手段，形式便于囤积、取用和交换。这些关于货币
创造和使用的描述，几乎仍见于每一本经济学教科书，与我们的日常经验相符。
en: What is money? The answer until recently seemed obvious. We thought of it as an object, in the shape of banknotes and coins, the everyday appearance it took in our hands. We associated its production largely with the powers of the modern state, since governments authorise the coining and printing of currency and establish the legal tender in which taxes and other debts must be paid. Economists conventionally defined its use in terms of three functions. It is a medium of exchange, enabling people to trade goods and services without resorting to barter; it is a unit of account, allowing business firms to record the prices of goods and calculate their profits; and it is a means of storing wealth, in a form that is easy to stockpile, retrieve, and exchange. These descriptions of
the creation and use of money, still found in almost every textbook of economics, corresponded to our ordinary experience.

zh: 然而今天，关于货币的正统和常识观点已被认为是不充分的。二十一世纪最初几十年的金融动荡，揭示出需要一种不同的理解。金融繁荣和房地产泡沫是由担保债务凭证和其他复杂货币产品的创造所推动的。
这些产品在 2007—8 年崩溃后引发的银行业危机，需要通过量化宽松的做法前所未有地创造银行信用。2020 年 3 月新冠疫情引发的流动性危机，导致信用货币更大幅度的扩张。在这些事件中，货币不仅是为了促进贸易或记账而被创造。它以新颖的方式、在新的尺度上被工程化。货币是一种装置，在其制造过程中，非凡形式的财富、不稳定和负债被创造出来。
en: Today, however, the orthodox and common-sense view of money is recognised as inadequate. The financial turbulence of the opening decades of the twenty-first century revealed the need for a different understanding. Financial booms and real estate bubbles were driven by the creation of collateralised debt obligations and other complex monetary products.

The banking crisis that followed the collapse of those products in 2007–8 required an unprecedented creation of bank credit, through the practice of quantitative easing. The liquidity crisis triggered by the Covid-19 pandemic in March 2020 led to an even larger expansion of credit money. In these events, money was not just created to facilitate trade or accounting. It was engineered in novel ways on a new scale. Money was a device in whose manufacture extraordinary forms of wealth, instability, and indebtedness were being created.

zh: 鉴于这些事件，一种对货币的不同理解出现了——或者更确切地说，被重新发现了。就其生产而言，政府创造的货币极少。尽管货币与国家货币和现代国家的权威相关联，但几乎所有货币的生产都不是政府财政部或中央银行的工作，而是公司利益集团的工作。在现代，商业银行获得了一种被经济学教科书大多忽视的巨大权力，可以大规模生产货币。就其用途而言，货币不仅是促进交换或提供财富储存手段的物品，而且是一种与未来的关系。它作为信用而产生，即对延期支付或未来商品的当下权利。无论其进一步用途如何，货币的起源和主要重要性在于索取未来收入，并且——这对我们所谓的资本主义至关重要——把这种未来索取权资本化，使其在当下以折价形式可得。
en: In light of these events, a different understanding of money has emerged – or, rather, has been rediscovered. In terms of its production, very little money is created by the government. Despite its association with national currencies and the authority of modern states, the production of almost all money is the work not of government treasuries or central banks but of corporate interests. In modern times, commercial banks have acquired an immense power, largely ignored by the textbooks of economics, to mass produce money. In terms of its use, money is not just an object that facilitates exchange or provides a means of storing wealth, but a relation to the future. It comes into being as credit, or the present right to a deferred payment or good. Whatever its further uses, the origin and main importance of money lies in claiming a future income and, crucial to what we call capitalism, capitalising that future claim and making it available at a discount in the present.

zh: 然而，正如我们将看到的，银行并非单独行动创造货币。如果未来没有被组织成可靠的支付来源，对未来支付的索取权就不会有效。银行只有在更广泛的未来攫取机制中，才获得制造货币的权力。这些机制包括贸易、基础设施和制造业的形式，法律及其执行系统，以及衡量、预测和简化当下与未来关系的装置。金融常与未来的另一个方面相关，即其不确定性。
然而，不确定性只有在作为从对未来的有效支配力内部产生并调节这种支配力的要素时，才具有重要意义。
en: As we will see, however, banks do not create money by acting alone. A claim on a future payment would be ineffective if that future was not organised as a reliable source of payment. Banks acquire the power to manufacture money only as part of wider mechanisms for the capture of the future. Those mechanisms include forms of trade, infrastructure, and manufacturing, systems of law and its enforcement, and devices that measure, forecast, and simplify the relation between the present and the future. Finance is often associated with a different aspect of the future, its uncertainty.
However, uncertainty is significant only as an element that arises from within, and modulates, an effective power over the future.

zh: 尽管新近才可见，这种把货币理解为对未来商品或支付的有效索取权、因而是一种支配未来的权力关系的观点并不新鲜。我们可以回到一百多年前的二十世纪初，当时货币的现代权力首次被清晰阐述，并克服经济学中因遗忘这项工作而来的“失去的世纪”。
被遗忘的关键文本之一，是 1913 年一篇题为“什么是货币？”的短文。
其作者阿尔弗雷德·米切尔—英尼斯最初不是在纽约或伦敦，而是在开罗了解现代金融的。他在英国占领时期于那里度过了职业生涯的形成期，担任埃及财政部副部长。
正如我们在前几章所见，那些年的埃及是新形式信用货币发展的重要场所。
en: Although newly visible, this understanding of money as an effective claim on future goods or payments, and thus a relation of power over the future, is not new. We can turn back more than a hundred years to the early twentieth century, when the modern powers of money were first clearly articulated, and overcome the ‘lost century’ in economics that followed the forgetting of this work.
One of the key forgotten texts is a short essay of 1913 entitled ‘What Is Money?’

Its author, Alfred Mitchell-Innes, had first learned about modern finance not in New York or London, but in Cairo. He spent the formative years of his career there during the British occupation, serving as under-secretary at the Egyptian Ministry of Finance.
As we saw in the previous chapters, Egypt in those years was an important site for the development of new forms of credit money.

zh: 1908 年，米切尔—英尼斯结束在开罗的任务后，被派往华盛顿。
五年后，他在《银行法杂志》上发表了“什么是货币？”。次年，在“许多经济学家和大学教授”反对他的观点后，该杂志编辑邀请他发表第二篇文章，更详细地阐述他所说的“货币信用理论”。
约翰·梅纳德·凯恩斯刚刚完成他自己第一项关于货币的研究《印度货币与财政》，他称赞米切尔—英尼斯的工作表明，传统的货币史“纯属神话”。
约瑟夫·熊彼特——我们知道他也曾与米切尔—英尼斯在同一时期短暂在开罗工作——已于 1911 年用德文发表了自己版本的货币信用理论，尽管其英译本《经济发展理论》直到 1934 年才问世。
en: After ending his assignment in Cairo, in 1908 Mitchell-Innes was posted to Washington.
He published ‘What Is Money?’ in

five years later. The following year, after ‘many economists and college professors’ objected to his views, the journal’s editor invited him to publish a second article, spelling out in more detail what he termed ‘The Credit Theory of Money’.
John Maynard Keynes, who had just completed his own first study of money,
, praised the work of Mitchell-Innes for showing that the conventional history of money ‘is quite mythical’.

Joseph Schumpeter, who as we know had also worked briefly in Cairo in the same period as Mitchell-Innes, had published his own version of the credit theory of money in German in 1911, although its English translation,
, did not appear until 1934.

zh: “什么是货币？”揭示了两大谬误。第一种认为货币的价值来自黄金或白银。尽管纸币的使用远比硬币和金银条广泛，但据称货币所基于的黄金或白银“本位”被认为决定了它的价值，并使一种货币的数量能够用另一种货币来衡量。这种观念主导了十九世纪的经济思想，但在二十世纪中叶后基本被放弃。
第二种谬误常被错误地归于亚当·斯密，在米切尔—英尼斯揭穿它之后又盛行了百年，它把货币的起源和目的解释为提供促进交换的手段。早期社会通过物物交换交易商品。随着商业扩张，人们通过发展货币作为交换媒介，克服了用一种商品交换另一种商品的不便。
en: ‘What Is Money?’ exposed two fallacies. The first held that money derived its value from gold or silver. Even though paper notes were used far more widely than coins and bullion, the gold or silver ‘standard’ on which money was said to be based was thought to determine its worth, and to allow a quantity of one currency to be measured against another. This idea had governed economic thinking in the nineteenth century but was to be largely abandoned after the mid-twentieth.

The second fallacy, often attributed falsely to Adam Smith and prevailing for another hundred years after Mitchell-Innes debunked it, explained the origin and purpose of money as providing a means to facilitate exchange. Early societies traded goods by barter. As commerce expanded, people overcame the inconvenience of bartering one good for another by developing the use of money as a medium of exchange.

zh: 米切尔—英尼斯表明，现有历史证据不支持这两种观点。第一，直到现代，人们从未试图用金属本位来定义“镑”“第纳尔”“美元”或任何其他货币的价值。这些名称表示记账单位。它们不是具有确定大小和重量的固定物体。统治者可能定期发行的金属硬币——通常用于支付士兵或其他服务，并作为税款收回——是其价值会变化的代币。金属货币在任何货币安排中都只占很小部分。它并不决定商人账目中记录的金额价值，而这些账目通常代表着最大、最稳定的货币体系。
en: The available historical evidence, Mitchell-Innes showed, supported neither of these views. First, until modern times, no attempt was made to define the value of a ‘pound’, a ‘dinar’, a ‘dollar’, or any other money in terms of a metallic standard. These names denoted units of account. They were not fixed objects of a determined size and weight. The metal coins that rulers might periodically issue, typically to pay for soldiers or other services, and to reclaim as tax payments, were tokens whose worth varied. Metal-based money was a minor part of any monetary arrangement. It did not determine the value of the sums recorded in the accounts of merchants, which usually represented the largest and most stable system of money.

zh: 第二，货币并非作为物物交换的便利替代品出现，而是作为信用机制出现。信用的使用见于最早文明的记录。在农业社会，信用与作物周期相关。商人和有权势的家庭向农民提供以田间作物为担保的信贷，收获后偿还。
每当商业关系和商人权力增强，信用就发挥更大的作用。在中世纪伊斯兰世界，商人使用
（预购）的做法，以折扣价购买未来作物，或为应付政府的税款提供资金，作为创造信用货币并从中获利的手段。
同样，零售和批发业务通常也以信用进行。
“在大多数情况下，”一位十一世纪的主要穆斯林法学家写道，“只有赊销才能获得利润。”
印度—伊斯兰世界的商人发展出为长途贸易延期支付的做法，广泛用于印度洋和阿拉伯地区的商业，后来传播到意大利，再传到欧洲其他地区。
这种方法通过一种在埃及和更广阔的阿拉伯世界被称为波斯术语
的装置创造货币。它在英语中被称为汇票。
en: Second, money emerges not as a convenient substitute for exchange by barter but as a mechanism of credit. The use of credit is found in the records of the earliest civilisations. In agrarian societies it was associated with the crop cycle. Merchants and other powerful households extended credit to farmers against the crop in the field, to be repaid with the harvest.
Credit assumed a greater role whenever commercial relations and the power of merchants intensified. In the medieval Islamic world, merchants used the device of
(forward buying) to purchase a future crop at a discount, or to cover a tax payment owed to the government, as a means of creating and profiting from credit money.
Likewise, both retail and wholesale business were routinely conducted on credit.
‘In most cases’, wrote a leading Muslim jurist of the eleventh century, ‘profit can only be achieved by selling for credit.’

The practice of deferred payment for long-distance trade, developed by merchants of the Indo-Islamic world and widely used in the commerce of the Indian Ocean and the Arab lands, spread to Italy and then the rest of Europe.
The method allowed the creation of money through a device that in Egypt and the wider Arab world was known by the Persian term
. It came to be known in English as a bill of exchange.

zh: 就最简单形式而言，汇票的运作如下。货物供应商需要预先得到付款，以生产或获取商品并安排运输。购买货物的商人通过开具一张作为欠条的汇票来创造一种信用——这个过程被称为“开立汇票”。汇票是承诺在未来某个日期付款的票据，名义上是货物应交付的日期；按照惯例，这段期限是标准的天数、周数或月数，取决于货物类型和运输距离。
承诺的可靠性——即汇票的可靠性——取决于
商人的声誉和实力。
这种实力通过诉诸法院和法律救济而延伸。在伊斯兰世界，法官及其法院在使商人能够发放信贷和收回欠款方面发挥了重要作用。
在欧洲，诉诸法官和法律调解的机会可能更为有限，早期现代国家的形成可以追溯到对更强有力的收债机制的需求。
en: In its simplest form, a bill of exchange works as follows. A supplier of goods requires to be paid in advance, to produce or acquire the merchandise and arrange its shipment. The merchant purchasing the goods creates a form of credit, by writing a bill of exchange as an IOU – the process known as ‘drawing a bill’. The bill is a promise to make the payment on a future date, nominally the date by which the goods are to be delivered and, by convention, a standard period of days, weeks, or months depending on the type of good and the distance it will travel.
The reliability of the promise – the soundness of the bill – rests on the
reputation and strength of the merchant.
This strength was extended through access to courts and legal remedies. In the Islamic world, judges and their courts played an important role in enabling merchants to extend and reclaim debts.

In Europe, where access to judges and the mediation of the law may have been more restricted, the formation of early modern states can be traced to the demand for stronger mechanisms for collecting debts.

zh: 未来付款的承诺变成一种可以立即交易的金融工具。如果汇票的持票人急需资金来偿还先前债务或购买更多货物，他可以把汇票签给另一个商人，作为支付手段。一旦同一张汇票可以多次由商人签转或背书，它就发挥支付系统的作用。
这种实践越是扩大——部分得益于索偿权的法律可执行性增强——它就变得越非个人化，越来越脱离特定的商人。这种脱离越深，支付装置的“货币性”就越强。尽管汇票与长途贸易有关，一种被称为“融通汇票”的变体提供了另一种创造信用的手段，其基础的商品销售是虚构的。
en: The promise of future payment becomes a financial instrument that can be immediately traded. A recipient of a bill who requires the funds right away, to settle an earlier debt or purchase further goods, can sign it over to another merchant as a means of payment. Once the same bill can be signed over, or endorsed, from merchant to merchant multiple times, it functions as a payment system.

The more the practice expands, thanks in part to the increasing legal enforceability of claims, the more impersonal it becomes, increasingly detached from specific merchants. The greater the detachment, the greater the ‘moneyness’ of the payment device. Although bills were associated with long-distance trade, a variant known as a ‘bill of accommodation’, where the underlying sale of goods was fictitious, provided a further means of creating credit.

zh: 并非所有信用都需要汇票。金融信用常常可能是非货币化信用和债务关系的延伸，在平常时期，这些关系构成了相互义务的结构，社会共同体正是通过它形成的。
当地货物供应商通常只需把债务记录在商人账簿中，或通过口头协议，就向零售客户或其他企业提供信用。
这种日常信用使用在欧洲资料中有广泛记载，在对中世纪和近代早期伊斯兰世界的研究中也同样明显。
与汇票不同，商人的账面信用不作为支付装置流通，也不总是与费用、折扣或利息支付相关。然而，信用余额可以通过开具本票来结清，本票作为信用货币在人们手中流转。
在欧洲，小企业也可能把账簿上的债务转换为汇票，尤其是那些长期未付的债务，或者它们也可能接受另一张汇票作为支付。
en: Not all credit required bills. Financial credit may often have functioned as an extension of non-monetised relations of credit and debt, which, in ordinary times, created the fabric of reciprocal obligation through which social community was forged.
Local suppliers of goods would typically extend credit to retail customers or other businesses by simply recording a debt in the merchant’s books, or by oral agreement.
Widely documented in European sources, this everyday use of credit is equally evident in studies of the medieval and early modern Islamic world.

Unlike bills of exchange, merchants’ book credit did not circulate as a payment device and was not always associated with a fee, discount, or interest payment. However, credit balances could be settled by writing promissory notes, which circulated from hand to hand as credit money.

In Europe, small businesses might also convert the debts on their books into bills of exchange, especially those obligations that went unpaid for long periods, or they might accept another bill in payment.

zh: 商人会在彼此之间结清汇票，许多债务和债权相互抵消，任何未结余额都转换为本票。铸币很少使用。
对于当地贸易，这种“结算”会偶尔进行，或者仅仅在账簿记满时进行。
历史上，定期集市
为来自不同地区的商人结算账目提供了场合。在东地中海，这种做法延续到现代。“不多年前，在埃及的集市上，”米切尔—英尼斯评论道，人们仍能看到大型集市——通常与宗教节日相关——如何充当商人的票据交换所。除了活跃的零售贸易，大多数商人在集市上的主要业务——例如在埃及三角洲坦塔举行的与赛义德·巴达维节相关的集市——是“债务与债权的结算”。
在近代早期欧洲，中世纪长途贸易的集市转变为“汇兑集市”，专门用于清算汇票。
据费尔南·布罗代尔所述，在最重要的集市、热那亚附近的皮亚琴察，每季度一次的票据交换和债务结算“支配了西方物质生活的节奏”。
en: Merchants would settle their bills among themselves, with many of the debts and credits cancelling one another out and any outstanding balance converted to a promissory note. Coinage was used only rarely.
For local trade, this ‘reckoning’ would happen on an occasional basis, or simply whenever an account book was full.
Historically, periodic fairs

provided the occasion for the settling of accounts between merchants from different regions. In the Eastern Mediterranean, this practice continued into modern times. ‘Not many years ago at the fairs of Egypt,’ Mitchell-Innes remarked, one could still see how large fairs, often associated with religious festivals, served as clearing houses for merchants. Alongside a brisk retail trade, the main business for most merchants at the fair – such as that associated with the feast of Sayyid Badawi held at Tanta in the Egyptian Delta – was ‘the settlement of debts and credits’.
In early modern Europe, the trade fairs of medieval long-distance trade were transformed into ‘exchange fairs’, dedicated to the clearing of bills.

According to Fernand Braudel, the quarterly exchange of paper and settling of debts at the most important of the fairs, at Piacenza, near Genoa, ‘dictated the rhythm of the material life of the West’.

zh: 这里的“西方”指位于印度—伊斯兰世界伟大贸易路线和商业中心边缘的一组城邦和王国。这种边缘位置使欧洲商人，尤其是热那亚的汇兑银行家，与货币形成了一种不同寻常的关系，并获得了从其创造中获利的机会。与其他地方一样，商人银行家与王公们共存，后者试图通过垄断铸造金银币的权利来巩固对城市和领地的控制。尽管铸币在货币体系中通常只起很小作用，但从十六世纪起，拉丁欧洲的贵金属承担了不同角色。商人冒险家开始把黄金和白银不作为货币，而作为主要贸易品，这几乎是他们可以用来交换亚洲织物、香料和其他奢侈品的唯一商品。与此同时，争相控制这种贸易并武装其参与者的王公们，需要越来越多的金银币来支付官员和雇佣兵。票据汇兑的做法与贵金属贸易交织在一起，使控制汇兑集市的人能够从日益复杂的汇兑关系中获利——往往通过腐败手段。到十七世纪初，这种复杂性和腐败促成了热那亚体系的崩溃。
欧洲对亚洲贸易路线的武装篡夺，使信用创造走上了一条不同的道路。但它很快又会再次转变。
en: ‘The West’ refers here to a collection of city-states and kingdoms located at the periphery of the great trade routes and commercial hubs of the Indo-Islamic world. The peripheral location gave European merchants, and especially the exchange bankers of Genoa, an unusual relation to money and the opportunities to profit from its creation. As elsewhere, merchant bankers coexisted with princes attempting to consolidate control over their cities and territories by monopolising the right to mint gold or silver coins. Although coinage typically played a small part in monetary systems, in Latin Europe from the sixteenth century, precious metals took on a different role. Merchant adventurers began to use gold and silver not as money but as a principal item of trade, almost the only commodity available to them to exchange for the fabrics, spices, and other luxury goods of Asia. At the same time, princes competing to control this trade and arm its protagonists required increasing access to gold and silver coinage, to pay their administrators and mercenaries. The practice of exchange by bills became entwined with trade in precious metals, allowing those who controlled the exchange fairs to profit – often corruptly – from the proliferating complexity of exchange relations. By the early seventeenth century, the complexity and the corruption helped bring about the collapse of the Genoese system.
Europe’s armed usurpation of Asian trade routes had set credit creation on a different path. But it would soon be transformed again.

zh: 货币成为折现的未来
en: Money Becomes the Discounted Future

zh: 随着欧洲长途贸易的主要路线及其日益增长的财富来源从地中海世界、黎凡特和红海转向大西洋和印度洋，欧洲货币创造的中心也从意大利转移到北方，先是十七和十八世纪的德国、安特卫普和阿姆斯特丹，然后到十九世纪的伦敦。
最大的英国商行——例如巴林家族，他们是来自英格兰西部的德国—荷兰裔棉花商人，以及罗斯柴尔德家族，他们先是在汉堡、后在曼彻斯特以布商身份发展业务——演变为商人银行家，专门交易和清算汇票，并承销和出售政府债务。
在十八和十九世纪，政府开始管制纸币发行，并指定一家国家银行或货币当局作为纸币的唯一发行者，把这些付款承诺转变为国家货币。英格兰作为该时期最成功的战争和殖民强国，开创了一种新颖的公私安排，由政府未来的税收收入保障纸币的价值。
然而，尽管集中印制的纸币成为一国法定货币的标志，它们在日常货币创造和供给中只起次要作用。随着私人银行从商人手中接管提供信用的主要角色，它们通过汇票、贷款和账簿余额创造货币——这些债务形式为购买未来商品和其他资产提供资金。这成为几乎所有货币的来源。
en: As the main routes of Europe’s long-distance trade and the source of its increasing wealth shifted from the Mediterranean world, the Levant, and the Red Sea to the Atlantic and Indian oceans, the hub of European money creation shifted from Italy to the north, first to Germany, Antwerp, and Amsterdam in the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries and then in the nineteenth century to London.

The largest English merchant houses – firms such as the Barings, who were cotton traders of German-Dutch origin from the English West Country, and the Rothschilds, who grew their business as cloth merchants first in Hamburg and then in Manchester – evolved into merchant bankers, specialising in trading and clearing bills of exchange and underwriting and selling government debt.

In the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries, governments began to regulate the issuing of notes, and to designate a national bank or monetary authority as the sole issuer of banknotes, transforming these promises to pay into national currencies. England, emerging as the most successful war-making and colonising power of that period, had pioneered a novel public–private arrangement, in which the government’s future tax revenues secured the value of paper money.

However, while centrally printed bank notes came to designate a country’s legal tender, they were to play only a minor role in the daily creation and supply of money. As private banks took over from merchants the main role in supplying credit, they created money through bills, loans, and ledger balances – forms of debt produced to fund the purchase of future goods and other assets. This became the source of almost all money.

zh: 以英国为例，随着工厂雇佣劳动的发展，大部分货币仍采取私人创造的信用形式。大雇主很少用现金支付工资，况且现金也很难找到。正如我们将看到的，他们用代金券、商店赊账或其他实物工资形式支付工人，但也用越来越多的私人“乡村”或地方银行发行的信用票据支付。
当政府限制地方银行发行票据时，个人支票支付成为纸币的主要形式。直到 1913 年，约翰·梅纳德·凯恩斯还评论说，在英国，支票是货币的主要形式，除了“某些自掏腰包的开支，例如铁路旅行，因为习俗要求现金支付”。
但在十九世纪下半叶现代银行业巩固之前，英国——如同欧洲其他地方——的多数
可即时使用的货币采取商店赊账、本票、地方私人银行票据和汇票的形式。
en: With the development of wage labour in factories, to remain with the case of Britain, most money continued to take the form of privately created credit. Large employers seldom paid wages in cash, which in any case was difficult to find. As we will see, they would pay workers in scrip, shop credit, or other forms of truck, but also with credit notes issued by the growing number of private ‘country’ or provincial banks.

When the government restricted the creation of notes by provincial banks, payment by personal cheque emerged as the main form of paper money. As late as 1913, John Maynard Keynes remarked that in Britain cheques were the principal form of money, except for ‘certain kinds of out-of-pocket expenditure, such as that on railway travelling, for which custom requires cash payment’.
But, before the consolidation of modern banking in the second half of the nineteenth century, most
ready money in Britain, as elsewhere in Europe, took the form of shop credit, promissory notes, local private bank notes, and bills of exchange.

zh: 理解货币作为信用而产生，不仅对金融史重要。信用货币是一种社会和技术关系，建立在当下确立并向前延伸的权力之上，以控制未来应偿还的债务。虽然货币体系也可以提供记账手段，但其主要目的源于创造一种以可靠的强制执行手段确保在未来偿付的债务。那个被强制执行的未来，是一个通过技术政治过程构建和控制的世界，它塑造生活方式和繁荣形式。货币不仅是代表价值或润滑某种更真实过程的物品。它是一种攫取的技术装置。然而，这种装置的力量部分在于它显得仅仅是一种抽象物，是更真实对象或过程的单纯符号或代表。
en: Understanding that money comes into being as credit matters not just for the history of finance. Credit money is a social and technical relation, built upon a power established in the present and extending forwards, to control a debt to be paid in the future. While a monetary system may also provide a means of keeping accounts, its main purpose derives from creating a debt that is paid forwards through a means of reliable enforcement. That enforced future is a world that is constructed and controlled through a technopolitical process, in ways that shape patterns of living and forms of prosperity. Money is not simply an object representing value or lubricating some more real process. It is a technical apparatus of capture. However, the strength of the apparatus rests in part on appearing as only an abstraction, the mere token or representation of a more real object or process.

zh: 当这种跨时间关系规模化组织时，它成为债权人重要收入的来源。收益来自所谓的“贴现”实践。
货币是对未来资产或债务的当下索取权。由于获取该资产或债务支付的机会在未来，愿意接受汇票作为当前债务清偿的商人或金融商行，可以通过支付低于面值的价格来获得它。以较低价格购买汇票或未来付款承诺，被称为对汇票“贴现”。
en: When organised at scale, this relation across time becomes the source of significant income to the creditor. The gain arises from the practice known as ‘discounting’.

Money is a present claim on a future asset or debt. Since access to that asset or debt payment lies in the future, the merchant or finance house willing to take a bill of exchange as settlement for a current debt can acquire it by offering less than its face value. The purchase of a bill, or promise of future payment, at a lower price is known as ‘discounting’ the bill.

zh: 其运作如下。一位商人接受一张承诺——比方说——六个月后支付 100 英镑的汇票时，可能会把其价值贴现 5%。当下的贴现值反映了延期付款发生前的时间延迟，以及这笔款项可能永远无法兑现的小风险。（那些后来被称为“贴现商行”的大型商人银行，可以通过持有庞大而多样化的票据组合，把接受汇票的风险降到最低。）持有 100 英镑汇票、急需用钱的人，只能从愿意接受汇票的商人那里得到 95 英镑。卖方满足了立即偿还先前债务或进行进一步采购的需要，代价是损失应得收入的 5%。此人以损失未来收入的形式付出代价。另一方面，以折扣价获得汇票的商人赚取了损失的那部分金额，用 95 英镑购买 100 英镑的收入。几乎不费力气，95 英镑的付款经过几个月就变成 100 英镑。汇票贴现大规模反复进行，成为重要且几乎无成本利润的来源。
en: This works as follows. A merchant accepting a bill that promises, say, a payment of £100 at a date six months in the future might discount its value by 5 per cent. The discounted value in the present reflects the delay in time until the deferred payment occurs, and the small risk that the payment might never materialise. (The large merchant banking houses, which came to be known as ‘discount houses’, could minimise the risk in accepting bills by maintaining a large and diverse portfolio.) The owner of the £100 bill who needs to spend the funds right away receives only £95 from the merchant willing to take it. The seller satisfies a need to pay off an earlier debt or make a further purchase immediately, at the cost of losing 5 per cent of the income due. That person pays a penalty in the form of a loss of future earnings. The merchant who acquires the bill at a discount, on the other hand, gains that lost amount, purchasing £100 of income for £95. For the expenditure of little or no effort, a payment of £95 is transformed by the passage of a few months into £100. Repeated on a wide scale, the discounting of bills became the source of significant and almost costless profits.

zh: 正如我们在
所见，二十世纪的经济学家，尤其是美国的经济学家，逐渐把这种收益视为对“货币的时间价值”的回报，仿佛时间是货币的自然属性。但创造获利机会的推迟或延迟，并非简单的自然现象。延迟机制必须被工程化。
en: As we saw in

, economists in the twentieth century, especially in the United States, came to see this gain as a reward for ‘the time value of money’, as if time were a natural property of money. But the postponement or delay that creates the opportunity for gain is not a simple phenomenon of nature. The mechanism of delay had to be engineered.

zh: 长途贸易的进行，为创造信用货币提供了不断扩大的机会。通过在购买与交货之间打开显著的时间缺口，异地交换产生了推迟或中断，汇票贴现者可以从中获利。随着延迟和贴现机会的激增，创造信用货币成为贸易的目的。
大商人或商人银行的目标越来越不是获取商品并从异地的转售中获利，而是组织商品流动，以创造信用创造的机会，并从开立（创造）汇票与其付款之间的时间延迟中获利。距离和延迟迫使供应商接受汇票的折价，而商人或银行商行则从以折扣价获得未来付款中获利。大商人不是组织信用来促进贸易流动，而是组织贸易来促进信用创造。
en: The conduct of long-distance trade provided an expanding opportunity to create credit money. By opening a significant gap in time between a purchase and its delivery, non-local exchange generated the deferral or interruption from which a discounter of bills could make a gain. As the opportunities for delay and discounting proliferated, the creation of credit money became the purpose of trade.

The goal of the large merchant or merchant bank was increasingly not to acquire goods and profit from their resale in a different location. It was to organise the movement of goods in order to create opportunities for the creation of credit, and to profit from the delay in time between the drawing (creating) of a bill and its payment. The distance and delay forced the supplier to accept a discounted price for the bill, and the merchant or banking house profited from acquiring future payments at a discount. Rather than organising credit to facilitate the flow of trade, large merchants organised trade to facilitate the creation of credit.

zh: 货币不仅仅是某种更真实事物的代表。它构成一种从未来获取收入的机制；在这个日益被组织起来——正如我们将看到的——以创造延迟和推迟形式的世界里，这些形式把未来设定为有利可图的抽取场所。
en: Money is not the mere representation of something more real. It forms a mechanism for acquiring income from the future, in a world increasingly organised, as we will see, to create forms of delay and postponement that set up the future as a place for profitable extraction.

zh: 制造
en: Fabrication

zh: 正如前几章所示，我们不应把资本视为从过去积累起来的东西，而应视为从未来索取的东西。它代表的不是财富储备的积累，而是对预期付款的控制。
这种视角转变乍看意味着我们放弃了具体、物质关系的研究。它意味着把注意力从物质转向投机，从真实转向虚构。如果资本是一种与未来的关系，与尚未发生的事情的关系，那么它似乎建立在猜测和虚构之上，而不是建立在活生生的人类之间物质生活的实际生产之上。这种关于我们
与时间关系的思想——未来是虚构的，只有过去是真实的——难以理解组织集体世界的当代方式。它反映了一种幼稚的历史思维模式：过去是已知事件和安排的事实序列，而未来主要作为预测存在——根据对过去的了解可能推测出的一系列“结果”。

这种简单的历史主义不会让我们走得很远。我们已经知道，过去是被建构出来的——这里取fabrication一词积极的、制作与构建的含义。它是一组当下的指涉、记忆、报告、档案、遗产、痕迹和效果，我们试图组织、缓和并领会其力量。未来同样具有当下性。如果它是一种投射或建构，那它也是以具体方式被构建和投射的：人们在当下组织它、计算它、据此行动，并使它成为可供利用的东西。因此，目标不是放弃物质叙述——或者更好的说法，技术政治叙述——而是像关注过去的效果那样，关注未来被建构出来的效果。
en: We should think of capital, as previous chapters have shown, not as something accumulated from the past but as what is claimed from the future. It represents not the building up of a store of wealth, but the controlling of prospective payments.

This change in perspective suggests, at first, that we are abandoning the study of concrete, material relations. It implies refocusing attention from the material to the speculative, from the real to the fictitious. If capital is a relationship to the future, to something that has not yet happened, it seems to be built on conjectures and fabrications, rather than on the actual production of material life among living humans. Such thinking about our

relationship to time, where the future is fictitious and only the past is real, has difficulty making sense of contemporary ways of organising the collective world. It reflects a naive historical mode of thought, in which the past is a factual sequence of known events and arrangements, while the future exists mainly as prognosis – the range of possible ‘outcomes’ that might be conjectured from a knowledge of the past.

This simple historicism will not get us far. We already know that the past is a fabrication, in the positive sense of that word. It is a present set of references, memories, reports, archives, legacies, traces, and effects whose force we attempt to organise, mitigate, and apprehend. The future is no less present. If it is a projection or fabrication, it is fabricated and projected in concrete ways that are organised, calculated, acted upon, and made available in the current moment. The aim, then, is not to abandon a material account – or better, a technopolitical one. It is to be as attentive to the fabricated effects of the future as we have been to the effects of the past.

zh: 技术政治叙述可以区别于以物质生活生产为中心的历史叙述。理解资本的生产主义路径实际上也从未来开始，正如我们已经指出的，但那只是人类需求的未来。那些被假定的需求创造了一种需求，即提供维持人类生命所需之物的需求。物质需求通过组织生产过程得到满足。资本主义产生于这些生产过程的发展。在这种生产主义历史的核心，人们发现的不是通过在当下攫取预期收入而使未来负债的方法，而是改变当下生产物质商品以满足未来需求的方法。它的典型制度是生产商品的大型场所——现代工厂。它的典型支配形式是雇佣劳动，或由此产生的各种抽象。它的决定性事件是工业革命。
en: A technopolitical account can be distinguished from an account centred in the mere production of material life. The productivist approach to understanding capital actually starts in the future, as we already noted, but only a future of human needs. Those assumed needs create a demand, the demand to provide what is required to sustain human life. The material demand is met by organising processes of production. Capitalism arises from the development of those productive processes. At the centre of this productivist history, one finds not the methods of indebting the future by capturing prospective income in the present, but the transformation of present methods of producing material goods to meet the needs of the future. Its characteristic institution is the large-scale site of the production of goods, the modern factory. Its archetypal form of domination is wage labour, or the abstractions to which this gives rise. And its defining event is the industrial revolution.

zh: 然而，如果我们把这一事件视为攫取未来方式的转变，它就具有不同的意义。这种转变使英国和欧洲在那些转型中的角色去中心化，有助于更好地理解殖民、战争和奴隶制在现代形成中的位置。它也使我们能够重新定位雇佣劳动——正如我们将看到的——不是作为支配借以发生的抽象之来源，而是作为另一种生产债务关系的装置，未来正是通过这些关系被施加负担，并在当下被攫取。
en: That event, however, takes on a different import if we approach it as a shift in modes of capturing the future. The shift decentres the role of Britain and Europe in those transformations, contributing to a better understanding of the place of colonisation, war-making, and slavery in the shaping of the modern era. And it allows us to resituate wage labour, as we will see, not as the source of the abstraction through which domination occurs, but as another apparatus for the production of debt relations through which the future is encumbered and captured in the present.

zh: 英国工业革命的故事广为人知——其重要性也仍然常常被夸大。从 1780 年代到 1830 年的五十年间，英格兰西北部的纺织商人先重组了棉纱的纺制，最终重组了布匹的织造。他们摆脱了亚麻和羊毛行业以及加工来自奥斯曼帝国和印度的进口棉布时所使用的外放制，直接控制了大批工人，把他们聚集在水力“工厂”中（通常由其他用途改造而来），操作纺纱机和织布机，利用曼彻斯特周围山丘中湍急的溪流。乡村位置保证了低成本强制劳动力的供应，其中大多是儿童，由急于把贫民从账簿上划掉、把他们运往乡村教区的不断扩张的城市贫民习艺所提供。这些工厂生产的棉纱和后来的棉纺织品数量迅速增加。原棉没有一磅是当地种植的，成品布料也很少在本土消费，当地人仍偏好质量更好的羊毛和亚麻织物，或更精细的印度和波斯织物。较不耐用、质量较低的机器织棉布大多运往国外，最初是欧洲、西非以及加勒比和美国南方的奴隶种植园，后来是中东、南亚和世界其他地区。
en: The story of the industrial revolution in Britain is widely known – and its significance still often exaggerated. Within a span of fifty years, from the 1780s to 1830, textile merchants in northwest England reorganised first the spinning of cotton yarn and eventually the weaving of cloth. Moving away from the putting-out system used in the linen and woollen trades and in finishing imported cottons from the Ottoman Empire and India, they took direct control of large groups of workers, who were assembled in water-powered ‘mills’ (often repurposed from other uses) to operate spinners and looms that took advantage of fast-flowing streams in the hills around Manchester. The rural location guaranteed a supply of low-cost, forced labour, mostly children, provided by expanding urban poorhouses anxious to move paupers off their books by shipping them to rural parishes. The mills produced rapidly increasing quantities of cotton yarn and later cotton textiles. None of the raw cotton was grown locally, and little of the finished fabric was consumed at home, where the preference continued for better-quality woollens and linens, or the finer Indian and Persian fabrics. The less durable, low-quality machine-woven cotton fabric was mostly shipped abroad, initially to Europe, West Africa, and the slave plantations of the Caribbean and the American South, and later to the Middle East, South Asia, and the rest of the world.

zh: 对这种不同寻常安排的传统叙述，关键在于技术的作用，而技术常常充当资本的托词。它们把工业化（在某些解释中，还有先行的农业革命）视为由迅速而持续的技术创新所驱动的转变。这些叙述的不同之处主要在于这种驱动力的原因。相互竞争的解释将它分别归于：剩余资本的积累；自由或无财产的劳动力的获得所引起的生产者竞争；主要由儿童和妇女组成的大量贫困劳动力；创造勤奋精神的新消费文化；执行产权的有效法律制度的兴起；人口增长和土地可用性限制造成的生态压力；以及对殖民地和奴隶种植园的特权性准入——这些地方既生产原棉，又消费制成品。
en: Traditional accounts of this unusual arrangement turn on the role of technology, which functions so often as an alibi of capital. They see industrialisation (and, in some explanations, an antecedent agricultural revolution) as a transformation driven by rapid and continuous technical innovation. The accounts differ mainly in the reasons for this drive. Rival explanations attribute it variously to an accumulation of surplus capital, the competition among producers caused by access to free or propertyless labour, an abundant pauperised workforce of mainly children and women, a new culture of consumption creating a spirit of industriousness, the rise of an effective legal regime enforcing property rights, ecological pressures caused by a rising population and limits to the availability of land, and privileged access to colonies and slave plantations that both produced the raw cotton and consumed the manufactured textiles.

zh: 这些叙述把焦点放在棉纺厂及其机械上，并不令人意外。随着生产规模扩大，专门建造的工厂变成巨大而壮观的结构，成为景观中的新特征，其中一些甚至保留至今。曼彻斯特地区最著名的工厂之一，是
柴郡威尔姆斯洛附近的奎里班克纱厂（Quarry Bank Mill），如今是英国最大保护组织英国国民信托拥有的工业遗产地。
它建于 1784 年，后来发展成为世界上最大的棉纺织厂之一。今天它是一座关于工业革命的博物馆和档案馆，甚至是一部阴郁的英国电视剧的场景，编剧根据该遗址档案中的文件发展了故事。
来自该档案馆的史料出现在几乎所有关于英国工业革命的学术史中。用于构建那段历史的其他广泛使用的史料，包括工厂检查员的报告和机械发明的专利，都把故事聚焦于技术创新和工厂生产组织。
像奎里班克纱厂这样的大型纱厂实际上并不代表制造业；制造业在大多数情况下是在较小的场所发展起来的，但这些大厂给访客留下了印象，并受益于“维多利亚时代把‘资本’的力量物化并放大的倾向”，也受益于恩格斯、马克思和桑巴特等德国作家“执迷于把
（大企业）与高度资本主义时代联系起来”的做法。
纱厂加工的原棉以及生产的纱线和布匹，为编写一部聚焦于物质商品生产转变的历史提供了更多有形的材料。棉花的故事把更广阔的世界带入这部物质史。加勒比、美国南方、印度和埃及被组织起来生产棉花，按照标准叙述的说法，被纳入一个以工业生产为中心的世界经济。
en: The focus of accounts on the cotton mill and its machinery is no surprise. As the scale of production expanded, the purpose-built mills became large, imposing structures, forming new features in the landscape, some of which survive even today. One of the most well known of the Manchester-area factories, Quarry Bank Mill near Wilmslow in
Cheshire, is now an industrial heritage site owned by Britain’s biggest conservation organisation, the National Trust.

Built in 1784, it grew into one of the largest cotton-manufacturing plants in the world. Today it is a museum and archive of the industrial revolution, and even the setting of a grim British television drama series whose writers developed the story from documents in the site’s archive.

Sources from that archive figure in almost every scholarly history of the British industrial revolution. Other sources widely used to construct that history, including the reports of factory inspectors and patents for mechanical inventions, focus the story on technical innovation and the organisation of factory production.

Large mills like Quarry Bank were not actually representative of manufacturing, which, in most cases, developed in smaller establishments, but they made an impression on visitors, and benefited from ‘the Victorian disposition to reify and magnify the power of “capital”’, and from ‘the obsessive association of the
’, or large enterprise, with the age of high capitalism by German writers like Engels, Marx, and Sombart.

The raw cotton that the mill processed and the yarn and cloth it produced provide further tangible matter for composing a history focused on the transformation in the production of material goods. The story of cotton brings the wider world into this material history. The Caribbean, the southern United States, India, and Egypt were organised to produce the cotton, becoming incorporated, as the standard accounts put it, into a world-economy centred on industrial production.
body.review: 校注：底本德语拼作Grossbetreib；《杜登》所列“大企业”一词为Großbetrieb，词尾应为betrieb而非betreib。正文底本拼写照录。 https://www.duden.de/rechtschreibung/Groszbetrieb

zh: 这种以机器为焦点、以生产为中心、以英国为基础的现代资本主义起源叙述，已经受到一段时间的质疑。它有几个弱点。棉花的故事指的是一个小飞地，即便在英国也不代表大多数工业的组织方式或工人受雇方式。即使在纺织业中，对于大多数织物而言，外放制在很长时间内仍更有利可图，非机械化生产也大幅增加；许多企业领域继续使用手工劳动而没有大规模机械化，包括造船、酿造、吹玻璃、造纸、皮革加工、建筑业，以及大多数煤矿和炼铁。
棉花生产在另一种意义上也是一个飞地。与这一时期大多数英国和欧洲工业不同，其原料和大部分成品都不是本地的。正如我们刚才指出的，英国不种植棉花，而多达四分之三的纱线和制成布料——在其生产国是一种“薄得无法单独穿着”的织物——被出口。
正如一家曼彻斯特商行所描述的，这个行业以这种反常方式作为世界
商业的“怪胎”运作，与当地生活的其他领域联系薄弱，包括用当地羊毛和亚麻制成的更受欢迎、质量更好的织物。
事实上，正如贝克特所指出的，棉花作为一种既在欧洲之外生产（作为原料）又在欧洲之外消费的商品，其反常性恰恰意味着它特别适合全球资本化过程；具体而言，正如我们将看到的，适合大规模制造信用所需的错位。
en: This machine-focused, production-centred, British-based account of the genesis of modern capitalism has been questioned for some time. It has several weaknesses. The story of cotton refers to a small enclave, not representative, even in Britain, of how most industry was organised or workers were employed. Even in textiles, the putting-out system long remained more profitable for most fabrics, and non-mechanised production increased vastly; many areas of enterprise continued to use hand labour without large-scale mechanisation, including ship building, brewing, glass-blowing, paper making, leather work, the building trades, and most coal mining and iron smelting.

Cotton production was an enclave in another sense. Unlike most British and European industry in this period, the raw material and most of the final product were non-local. As we just noted, no cotton was grown in Britain, while up to three-quarters of the spun yarn and manufactured cloth, a fabric ‘too flimsy to be worn by itself’ in its country of fabrication, was exported.
Operating abnormally in this way as a ‘freak’ of world
commerce, as a Manchester firm described it, the industry had weak linkages with other areas of local life, including the more popular and better-quality textiles made from local wool and linen.

Indeed, as Beckert notes, the very abnormality of cotton, as a commodity that was both produced (as raw material) and consumed outside Europe, meant it was suited uniquely to the global process of capitalisation; and specifically, as we will see, to the dislocation required for the large-scale manufacture of credit.

zh: 关于以技术进步解释资本主义的传统，人们还指出了许多其他问题。正如我们在
和
所见，这类叙述常常忽视资本化对废物生产的偏好。棉花就是一个例子。它所取代的当地织物更耐久、更易修补；尤其是羊毛，不需要那么频繁地洗涤，因为它能吸收而不是困住身体的水分，而且与棉花不同，它天然抗菌。
相比之下，棉花的单薄及其产品的一次性，有利于频繁更换，因而有利于资本化所依赖的收入耐久性。更一般地说，与所谓工业革命相关的生产和财富的迅速增长，大部分并不是技术转型的结果。事实上，其中大部分可以归因于人口增长。机械化并没有产生物质增长。
这一时期的一项关键转型——从水力工厂到燃煤蒸汽机——的驱动力不是寻求技术改良，正如安德烈亚斯·马尔姆所示，而是因为更具成本效益的水力需要一群协调一致的使用者共同开发公共资源，而煤炭供应可以由私人确保（并被资本化）。蒸汽机还使生产能够从乡村转移到城市，提供更大、更脆弱的劳动力池，而机器过程扩大了控制劳动力的机会；劳动力集中在工厂中，使其拥有越来越大的权力来扰乱生产，从而要求改善条件。
最后，其他地区——例如中国——面临类似的人口压力和改良机会，却走上了与生产机械化不同的道路。如果说有什么不同，欧洲的发展不是由物质或技术优势塑造的，而是由缺乏禀赋塑造的——只有对亚热带奴隶殖民地的占有除外，这些殖民地既提供了机械化所围绕的原料，也提供了相关产品的市场。
en: Many other issues have been noted regarding the tradition of explaining capitalism in terms of technical progress. As we saw in
and

, such accounts often overlook the preference of capitalisation for the production of waste. Cotton exemplifies this. The local fabrics it replaced were more durable and mendable; wool in particular required less frequent laundering, since it is able to absorb rather than trap moisture from the body, and unlike cotton it is naturally anti-bacterial.

In contrast, the flimsiness of cotton and the disposability of its products favoured frequent replacement and thus the durability of revenue on which capitalisation depends. More generally, the rapid increase in production and wealth associated with the so-called industrial revolution was for the most part not the result of technical transformation. Most of it, in fact, can be attributed to increases in population. Mechanisation did not produce material growth.

A key transformation of the period, from water-powered mills to coal-powered steam engines, was driven not by a search for technical improvement, as Andreas Malm has shown, but by the fact that the more cost-effective water power required the shared development of a public resource among a coordinated group of users, whereas the supply of coal could be secured (and capitalised) privately. Steam engines also allowed production to move from rural to urban locations, providing a larger, more vulnerable pool of labour, while the machine process expanded the opportunities for control of a workforce whose concentration in factories had given it an increasing power to disrupt production and thus demand improved conditions.

Finally, other regions, such as China, faced similar demographic pressures and opportunities for improvement but took a different path from the mechanisation of production. If anything, developments in Europe were shaped not by material or technical advantages but by a lack of endowments – except for the possession of sub-tropical slave colonies, which provided both a source and a market for the material around which mechanisation was organised.

zh: 这些问题早已使一种较少欧洲中心主义的工业化叙述成为可能；这种叙述不从非凡的技术改良、英国人的独特勤奋或对日益增多商品的简单需求中寻找对已发生之事的解释，并且更意识到偶然性因素。
如今有一种强有力的反叙述，用更具全球性的术语解释工业革命，将其与更早的长途贸易、殖民和种植园奴隶制的发展联系起来。在这些解释中，有一场关于工业革命融资所需信用或资本来源的重要辩论，包括大西洋奴隶制与夺取莫卧儿帝国资源的相对重要性。
然而，要恰当地使欧洲及其工业化去中心化，就需要改变这些辩论的术语。即使在最好的叙述中，商业或商人资本也仅仅为工业化铺路。它提供的金融仅仅“润滑”了向工业生产的过渡。
en: These issues have already allowed for some time a less Eurocentric account of industrialisation, one that does not seek explanations for what happened in exceptional technical improvement, the peculiar industriousness of the British, or a simple demand for increasing numbers of goods, and one that is more aware of the element of contingency.

There is now a strong counter-narrative explaining the industrial revolution in more global terms, in relation to the earlier development of long-distance trade, colonisation, and plantation slavery. Within those explanations, there is an important debate on the sources of credit or capital for financing the industrial revolution, including the relative importance of Atlantic slavery versus the capture of resources of the Mughal Empire.

However, to properly decentre Europe and its industrialisation, the terms of those debates need to be altered. Even in the best accounts, commercial or mercantile capital merely prepares the way for industrialisation. The finance it supplies simply ‘lubricates’ the transition to industrial production.

zh: 应该使我们关切的问题，不是工业化如何获得融资。如果沿用这些术语，问题就会是

children: 金融如何以及为何被工业化

zh: 。然而这些术语并不充分，因为它们似乎假定了“金融”与“工业”之间的区别，假定了仅仅是润滑剂的货币与它所润滑的真实“机器”之间的区别，因而假定了货币经济与“实体经济”之间的区别。在接下来两章中，我们将从“实体”一侧接近这些问题，考察经济的谱系。我们将通过我们称之为“经济化”的过程，考察先是“经济的”事物、然后是“经济”这一对象的出现。然而目前，从理解货币这一侧出发，我们将继续使用更具包容性的术语“资本化”，正是因为它不从金融与实体之间的对立出发，而是探讨这种区分如何被发明、部署和掩盖。
en: The question that should concern us is not how industrialisation was financed. If we were to keep with these terms, the question would be how and why

. These terms are inadequate, however, for they appear to assume the difference between ‘finance’ and ‘industry’, between money that is merely a lubricant and the real ‘machine’ that it lubricates, and thus between the monetary economy and the ‘real economy’. In the following two chapters we will approach these questions from the side of the ‘real’ and consider the genealogy of the economy. We will examine the emergence of first ‘the economic’ and then ‘the economy’ through processes we will identify as ‘economisation’. For now, however, working from the side of understanding money, we will continue with the more capacious term ‘capitalisation’, precisely because it does not start from an opposition between the financial and the real, but explores how that distinction has been invented, deployed, and disguised.

zh: 因此，我们在此关注的不是商业和“商业资本主义”，而是资本化，商业只是资本化和攫取未来收入的一种方式。由此我们可以进一步提出两个论点。这两个论点将把工厂制度的发展不是置于早期商业发展的顶点，而是置于一次
的后果之中；这次绕道是一种扰动，打乱了更广泛、较少以欧洲为中心的当下获取未来付款的方式。绕道的观念不仅暗示一种偶然性因素——多种发展相结合产生一个结果——而且暗示一个较少
线性的过程，其特征是延迟、中断和不连续。我们还将看到，工厂生产的一个显著特征如何使它出人意料地产生一种从未来抽取的新方式——一种更地方化的信用创造方法，它作为雇佣劳动运作，并被误认为雇佣劳动。在工资这一装置中，我们将发现，一种现代而极其简单的货币概念出现了。
en: By focusing here, then, not on commerce and ‘commercial capitalism’ but on capitalisation, where commerce is one mode of capitalising and capturing a future revenue, we can go on to propose two additional arguments. These will place the development of the factory system not as the culmination of earlier commercial developments but as the consequence of a

, a disturbance that unsettled the wider, less-European-centred modes of acquiring future payments in the present. The idea of a detour suggests not just an element of contingency, in which multiple developments combine to create an outcome, but a less

linear process characterised by delay, interruption, and discontinuity. And we will see how one notable feature of factory production allowed it to give rise, unexpectedly, to a new mode of extraction from the future – the more localised method of credit creation that operated and was misrecognised as wage labour. In the device of the wage, we will discover, there emerged a modern and very simple conception of money.

zh: 工业革命作为一次绕道
en: Industrial Revolution as a Detour

zh: 首先是绕道。英国商人早已习惯于从资助殖民贸易、战争和动产奴隶制中获得巨额利润，他们为何会选择不同寻常而艰辛的道路，在离家很近的地方把工人大规模组织进工厂？通过新的制造业控制来提高剩余，与从未来攫取收入有何联系？与其诉诸“技术改良”或“需求”增加的论点，不如从 1770 年代到 1820 年代发生的一场全球性资本化过程危机中寻找另一种答案；这一过程依赖于军事化贸易垄断、殖民和奴役。转向棉纺织，是为了挽救被全球战争、殖民扩张、抵抗和革命打乱的信用制造体系而采取的一次绕道。这场危机的一部分——发生在欧洲内部的发展——广为人知，尽管人们较少把它与其所联系的更广泛事件联系起来。但让我们从那里开始。
en: First, the detour. Why did British merchants, long accustomed to the large profits from financing colonial trade, warfare, and chattel slavery, take the unusual and laborious path of organising workers close to home on a large scale into factories? How was the raising of surplus through a new control over manufacturing connected with the capture of revenue from the future? Instead of resorting to arguments about ‘technical improvement’ or increasing ‘demand’, an alternative answer can be found in the worldwide crisis in the processes of capitalisation, dependent on militarised trading monopolies, colonisation, and enslavement, that occurred in the period from the 1770s to the 1820s. Cotton manufacture was the diversion taken to salvage a system of credit manufacture disrupted by global warfare, colonial expansion, resistance, and revolution. One part of this crisis is well-known, the developments occurring within Europe, although it is less often associated with the wider events to which it was connected. But let us start there.

zh: 1789 年凡尔赛三级会议召开后的几年里，革命席卷欧洲，伦敦的商人—金融家及其在欧洲的商业伙伴被迫把信用转用于纺织生产的扩张。这种转用既不能用消费者对更多布匹的突然需求来解释，也不能用寻找新投资的资本“剩余”来解释。它是商人金融发生错位的结果，需要一个新的过程来完成信用创造和获利所依赖的循环。
en: When revolution engulfed Europe in the years after the summoning of the Estates-General at Versailles in 1789, merchant-financiers in London and their business partners in Europe were forced to divert credit into the expansion of textile production. This diversion is explained neither by a sudden consumer demand for more cloth, nor by a ‘surplus’ of capital looking for new investments. It was the result of a dislocation of merchant finance, requiring a new process through which to complete the circulation that allowed the creation of and profit from credit.

zh: 1790 年代，法国革命战争蔓延欧洲，伦敦的商人债权人资助了欧洲大陆的战争。英国政府为德国各邦统治者提供的雇佣兵付费，扩展了美国独立战争期间发展起来的雇佣兵制度。这些战争付款的规模
前所未有。到拿破仑战争结束时，军费开支占英国政府收入的 58%。

政府以未来税收作抵押借款，付款不是用现金，而是通过以伦敦商人为付款人的信用证转移；这些商人在德国的代理或合伙人把资金用于招募和供应士兵。于是欧洲大陆的商人在伦敦积累了贷方余额。这些纸面财富只有通过找到把信用反向转移的办法才能变现，即用德国人在伦敦持有的票据购买英国货物，供应欧洲。（票据本身不移动：相反，为了平衡贷方和借方，并从其创造中获利，货物必须运回德国。）用于这种互补的信用流动和利润实现的主要载体，是纺织品的转移。虽然现有的英格兰毛织品和亚麻织品贸易可以提供部分信用转移机制，但疏通和扩大金融的主要手段，是让这些票据发挥作用，在英格兰发展另一种织物——棉布——的生产，而棉布此前主要从东方进口。用于资助欧洲大陆战争的伦敦票据，需要换上一身新衣才能回流。正如一位伦敦金融家 1811 年所言，被冻结的战时票据信用相当于“如此多的外国资本投资于英国工业”。
en: As the French revolutionary wars spread across Europe in the 1790s, London merchant creditors financed war on the continent. The British government paid for mercenaries supplied by the rulers of German states, extending a system of hired soldiery developed during the American Revolutionary War. The scale of these payments for warfare
was unprecedented. By the end of the Napoleonic wars, military spending was accounting for 58 per cent of the British government’s revenue.

Borrowing against future tax revenues, the government transferred the payments not in cash but via letters of credit drawn on London merchants, whose agents or partners in Germany made the funds available to recruit and supply the soldiers. The merchants on the continent thus accumulated credits in London. These paper fortunes could be realised only by finding ways to move credit in the reverse direction, by using the German-owned bills in London to purchase British goods to supply to Europe. (The bills themselves did not move: rather, to balance the credits and debts, and to profit from their creation, goods had to move back to Germany.) The main vehicle used for this complementary movement of credit and the realisation of profit was the transfer of textiles. While the existing trade in English woollens and linens could provide some of the machinery of credit transfer, the principal means of unblocking and expanding finance was to put the bills to work in developing the production in England of a different fabric, cotton, which until then had been largely imported from the East. The London bills used to fund the war on the continent required a new clothing to return. As a London financier remarked in 1811, the blocked credit of wartime bills amounted to ‘so much foreign capital invested in British industry’.

zh: 这一过程得益于商人从巴黎、阿姆斯特丹、汉堡和其他欧洲大陆贸易中心迁往伦敦。他们逃离革命势力，在其触及不到的地方建立商行，从资助货物运输的战时机会中获利。拿破仑在埃及战败后，法国实施大陆封锁体系，试图阻断与英国的贸易，这为有能力走私货物、突破封锁的人带来了额外利润。
据关于金融资本主义兴起的主要历史著作所述，这些由战争驱动的信用流动，以及创造和调动信用所需的货物流动，“简明地解释了”“英国工业革命为何发生在那个时期”。
en: The process was aided by the relocation of merchants from Paris, Amsterdam, Hamburg, and other trading centres on the continent to London. Fleeing the revolutionary forces and establishing trading houses outside their reach, the merchants profited from the wartime opportunities to finance the movement of goods. After Napoleon was defeated in Egypt, France imposed the Continental System in an attempt to block commerce with Britain, allowing additional profits for those with means to smuggle goods through the blockade.

These movements of credit driven by war, and of the goods required to create and mobilise credit, ‘explain succinctly’, according to the leading history of the rise of finance capitalism, ‘why the British industrial revolution took place during that period’.

zh: 内森·罗斯柴尔德的职业生涯说明了这种借助机器的绕道如何运作；他是这些流离失所的布商和金融家中最著名的一位。
他的父亲是法兰克福一位成功的商人，曾担任黑森—卡塞尔统治者的金融代理人，后者是英国雇佣兵的主要供应者。父亲通过经营该统治者的英国汇票发家，后来又为向奥地利皇室
供应战争物资提供融资。他的儿子内森在 1799 年左右被派往曼彻斯特，当时他二十出头，开始做棉布生意，把布匹运回法兰克福和欧洲其他城市。当时至少有八名德国商人定居曼彻斯特，他是其中之一，这个数字还在继续增加。
内森可以从处理他父亲票据生意英国一端的伦敦商行获得汇票——换言之，利用他父亲在伦敦积累的剩余欠条作为可即时使用的货币。这种获得充足信用货币的渠道，使他能够以低于其他曼彻斯特棉布商人的价格出售，后者通常用两到六个月到期的票据从当地织工那里购买布匹。内森通过“按即期票据条件”预付，可以找到“急需用钱”并愿意降价 15% 或 20% 的织工。
en: The career of Nathan Rothschild, one of the best known of these displaced cloth traders and financiers, illustrates this machinic diversion at work.

His father was a successful Frankfurt merchant who served as a financial agent for the ruler of Hesse-Kassel, the main supplier of mercenary troops to the British. The father built a fortune dealing in the ruler’s English bills of exchange, and later in financing the

supply of war matériel to the Austrian imperial court. His son Nathan was sent to Manchester around 1799, while still in his early twenties, to begin trading in cotton goods, shipping cloth back to Frankfurt and other cities in Europe. He was one of at least eight German traders to settle in Manchester around then, a number that continued to increase.

Nathan could obtain bills from the merchant houses in London that handled the British side of his father’s bill dealing – using, in other words, the surplus IOUs his father had built up in London as ready money. This access to plentiful credit money allowed him to undercut other Manchester cotton traders, who typically purchased cloth from local weavers with bills payable in two to six months. By paying upfront ‘on present bill terms’, Nathan could find weavers ‘in want of money’ and willing to lower their prices by 15 or 20 per cent.

zh: 罗斯柴尔德通过疏通需要伦敦对应票据的德国票据来采购布匹，这一成功意味着他很快就难以找到足够的供应。大约一年内，他与博尔顿—瓦特公司达成安排，购买一台绕纱机——一种木制装置，可以把供织机梭子使用的纱线同时卷绕到几根锭子上。通过向织工提供已经绕在锭子上的纱线，罗斯柴尔德提高了织工向他供应布匹的速度。绕纱机在充当加速布匹生产装置的同时，还有更多作用——它是一种改善信用货币流通的机制。积累在他位于法兰克福的父亲手中的汇票，如今可以投入使用了。
en: Rothschild’s success in buying via the unblocking of German bills in need of London counterparts meant he soon struggled to find sufficient supplies. Within about a year, he arranged with the firm of Boulton& Watt to purchase a copping machine, a wooden contraption that allowed the yarn for the weavers’ shuttles to be ‘copped’, or wound, onto several spindles at once. By supplying weavers with yarn already wound on the spindle, Rothschild increased the rate at which the weavers could supply him with cloth. While serving as a device to speed up the production of cloth, the copping machine was something more – a mechanism to improve the circulation of credit money. The bills of exchange accumulating in the hands of his father in Frankfurt could now be put to work.

zh: 几年之内，内森·罗斯柴尔德搬到伦敦，专注于贸易融资、汇票贴现，以及充当统治者的投资经纪人。通往曼彻斯特的绕道在疏通了信用流动之后，如今可以留给别人。曼彻斯特成为商人—金融家的中心，他们与周围乡村的纺织厂合作并投资，但“最重要的是……为贸易融资，充当制造供应商的付款人，并向海外客户提供长期信贷”。
在海外贸易中发挥主导作用的是定居曼彻斯特的外国人，尤其是德国商人，例如埃尔门—恩格斯公司；创始人之一的儿子弗里德里希·恩格斯在那里管理公司的商业交易、会计和情报收集。
这些情报有助于他朋友卡尔·马克思的写作，塑造了一种以曼彻斯特为中心的资本化过程论述。
en: Within a few years, Nathan Rothschild had moved to London, to focus on the financing of trade, the discounting of bills, and acting as investment broker to rulers. The detour to Manchester, having unblocked the flow of credit, could now be left to others. The city became the centre of merchant-financiers, who worked with and invested in the textile mills in the surrounding countryside but ‘above all . . . financed the trade, serving as paymasters to their manufacturing suppliers and extending long credits to their overseas customers’.

A dominant role in the overseas trade was played by foreigners settled in Manchester, especially German merchants, such as the firm of Ermen& Engels, where Friedrich Engels, the son of one of the founders, managed the firm’s commercial dealing, accounting, and intelligence gathering.
This intelligence helped inform the writing of his friend Karl Marx, shaping a Manchester-centred account of the capitalisation process.

zh: 随着德国商行的发展，来自奥斯曼世界的商人后来也日益增多——希腊人、

亚美尼亚人、阿拉伯人和土耳其人，他们在英国都被称为“希腊人”，为与伊兹密尔、阿勒颇、开罗和亚历山大等城市的贸易融资，后来又为与西非和大多数其他地区的贸易融资。在许多情况下，他们在海外城市建立了自己的分号。例如，由来自伊斯坦布尔的希腊商人家庭创办的曼彻斯特卡瓦菲公司（Cavafy and Co.），于 1840 年代在亚历山大开设了一家分号，由创办人的儿子之一彼得罗斯经营。（彼得罗斯去世、1870 年代的金融危机迫使家族关闭亚历山大分号后，家族回到了曼彻斯特。一位孙子又搬回亚历山大，兼职做股票交易所经纪人来赚钱，但作为时代变迁的标志，他在英国统治下的灌溉部工作了三十年，以此谋生——这份任职倒也恰如其分。从这个希腊商人世界的角落，“与宇宙成一个微小的角度”站立，他成为著名诗人 C. P. 卡瓦菲。）
来自奥斯曼世界的商人数量继续增长，到 1870 年，他们在主导曼彻斯特长途贸易的 400 名常驻外国商人中超过了德国人，成为最大的群体。
据一份当时的报道，曼彻斯特“被殖民化”了，殖民者正是这些外国商人。凭借他们的信用网络、贸易经验、对海外商法的理解以及多种语言知识，奥斯曼和其他商人群体是棉纺织业发展的“主要推动者”。
en: The growth of German merchant houses was later matched by the increasing number of traders from the Ottoman world – Greeks,

Armenians, Arabs, and Turks, all referred to in Britain as ‘Greeks’, who financed trade with cities like Izmir, Aleppo, Cairo, and Alexandria, and later with West Africa and most other regions. In many cases, they established their own branches in overseas cities. The Manchester firm of Cavafy and Co., for example, founded by a Greek merchant family from Istanbul, opened an Alexandria office in the 1840s, run by one of the founder’s sons, Petros. (The family returned to Manchester after the death of Petros and the financial crisis of the 1870s had forced the family to close the Alexandria office. A grandson moved back to Alexandria and made money on the side as a broker on the stock exchange, but, as a sign of the changing times, supported himself under the British by working for thirty years, appropriately enough, at the Ministry of Irrigation. From this corner of the Greek merchant world, standing ‘at a slight angle to the universe’, he became the noted poet C. P. Cavafy.)

The merchants from the Ottoman world continued to grow in number, and, by 1870, surpassed the Germans as the largest group among the 400 resident foreign merchants who dominated Manchester’s long-distance trade.

Manchester, according to a contemporary report, ‘came to be colonised’ by these foreign merchants. With their credit networks, trading experience, understanding of overseas commercial law, and knowledge of multiple languages, the Ottoman and other merchant communities were the ‘prime movers’ in the development of cotton manufacturing.
body.review: 校注：底本称彼得罗斯去世后家族回到曼彻斯特。奥纳西斯卡瓦菲档案馆的传记记述，诗人的母亲在1870年丈夫去世后携子女赴英，1872—1877年先住利物浦、后住伦敦，随后返回亚历山大。正文地名照录。 https://cavafy.onassis.org/creator/cavafy-c-p/

zh: 使曼彻斯特地方化
en: Provincialising Manchester

zh: 如果说曼彻斯特的外国商人为贸易提供融资，推动了向棉纺织业的绕道，那么其中的“希腊人”把这次绕道与奥斯曼世界，尤其是埃及和阿拉伯正在进行的转变联系起来。在离开欧洲—地中海世界之前，让我们简要追踪这一联系。拿破仑·波拿巴对埃及的短暂占领（1798—1801）本意是把该国变成法国殖民地，以弥补最近失去印度和北美殖民地，以及加勒比被奴役者起义可能带来进一步损失的威胁，尤其是法国最有价值的海外领地、也可能是世界上生产力最高的殖民地领土——圣多明各（海地）的糖业种植园殖民地。
马赛的法国航运利益集团
热切支持埃及冒险。他们的利润在于为东地中海贸易融资，这种商业在十八世纪上半叶曾短暂被他们主导（尽管他们对更富裕的奥斯曼内部贸易仍处于边缘），但如今正输给希腊、亚美尼亚和其他奥斯曼商行。
然而结果却截然不同：法国在尼罗河上建立一个海地的计划失败了，埃及则作为一个有别于其他地区的权力中心得到加强，相对于伊斯坦布尔的奥斯曼当局获得了越来越大的自主性。
en: If the foreign merchants of Manchester financed the trade that helped drive the detour into cotton manufacturing, the ‘Greeks’ among them connected that detour to transformations under way in the Ottoman world, especially Egypt and Arabia. Before leaving the European-Mediterranean world, let us briefly follow this connection. Napoleon Bonaparte’s short-lived occupation of Egypt (1798–1801) had been intended to make the country into a French colony, to compensate for the recent loss of colonies in India and North America and the threat of further losses from uprisings by enslaved people in the Caribbean, notably in France’s most valuable overseas possession, and possibly the most productive colonial territory anywhere in the world, the sugar plantation colony of Saint-Domingue (Haiti).
French shipping interests in Marseilles were

keen to support the Egyptian venture. Their profits lay in financing trade with the Eastern Mediterranean, a commerce they had briefly dominated in the first half of the eighteenth century (although they remained peripheral to the richer internal Ottoman trade), but were now losing to the Greek, Armenian, and other Ottoman merchant houses.

The result, however, was something very different: the defeat of the French plan for a Haiti-on-the-Nile and the strengthening of Egypt as a distinct centre of power, increasingly autonomous from the Ottoman authorities in Istanbul.

zh: 开罗的自主性在十八世纪后期已经增强，得益于奥斯曼日益分权化的治理政策。
像阿里贝伊·卡比尔这样的地方统治者开始压过对手执政家族，着手军事扩张，并鼓励商业增长、从中获利；埃及历史学家贾巴尔提注意到了这一发展，其标志是在布拉克——服务于开罗的河港——和坦塔等地建造大型商业综合体，后者盛大的季节性集市我们已经提到过。
对奥斯曼统治的另一个商业和政治挑战出现在阿拉伯半岛，穆罕默德·本·沙特治下的迪里耶酋长国与从事长途贸易的富有阿拉伯商人以及穆罕默德·伊本·阿卜杜勒·瓦哈卜的宗教改革运动结盟，将其权力从波斯湾扩展到红海，横跨整个半岛，控制了圣城麦加；麦加每年的布匹集市是印度洋世界最大的商业活动之一。

在拿破仑的干预之后，开罗在 1805 年至 1848 年统治的穆罕默德·阿里帕夏治下继续扩张。他建立了一支庞大的陆军和海军，镇压了阿拉伯半岛的瓦哈比运动，并进一步扩大统治，先征服苏丹诸王国，然后进军巴勒斯坦和叙利亚。为了获得新帝国，他从欧洲寻求武器和海军舰艇，这给了英国、希腊和其他商人——他们从阿勒颇和其他奥斯曼贸易中心被吸引到亚历山大——为供应主要进口品提供融资的机会，即埃及不断增强的战争能力所需的“军需品、木材和其他商品”。
en: Cairo’s autonomy had already been growing in the later eighteenth century, benefiting from an Ottoman policy of increasingly decentralised governance.

Local rulers like Ali Bey al-Kabir began to dominate rival governing households, embark on military expansion, and encourage and profit from increasing commerce, a development noted by the Egyptian historian al-Jabarti and marked by the building of large commercial complexes at sites like Bulaq, the river port serving Cairo, and Tanta, whose great seasonal fair has already been mentioned.

Another commercial and political challenge to Ottoman rule emerged in Arabia, where the Emirate of Dir’iya, under Muhammad bin Sa’ud, in alliance with wealthy long-distance Arab merchants and with the reformist religious movement of Muhammad ibn Abd al-Wahhab, extended its power across the entire peninsula from the Persian Gulf to the Red Sea, taking control of the holy city of Mecca, whose annual cloth fair was among the largest commercial events of the Indian Ocean world.

After the interruption by Napoleon, Cairo continued its expansion under Muhammad Ali Pasha, who ruled from 1805 to 1848. He built a large army and navy, crushed the Wahhabi movement in Arabia, and further expanded his rule, first over the kingdoms of Sudan and then to Palestine and Syria. To acquire the new empire, he sought arms and naval vessels from Europe, giving British, Greek, and other merchants, drawn to Alexandria from Aleppo and other Ottoman trading centres, the opportunity to finance the supply of the main imports, namely ‘warlike stores, timber, and other commodities’ required for the expanding Egyptian powers of war-making.
body.review: 校注：本段将迪里耶政权的扩张合并叙述在穆罕默德·本·沙特治下。Saudipedia记其统治止于1765年，并将此后跨半岛扩张分别置于继任者阿卜杜勒阿齐兹及沙特治下，故此处不宜理解为所列扩张均由创立者在世时完成。正文保留原作概述。 https://saudipedia.com/en/first-saudi-state

zh: 为一个尼罗河上的新强国扩张提供融资，又造就了另一股需要取道兰开夏棉纺厂的力量。穆罕默德·阿里以信用购买武器和其他战争物资，信用由这些商人垫付，尤其是英国布里格斯公司（Briggs & Co.）。为了获得信用，帕夏也以自己的信用支付，形式是未来
交付作物的合同。
但哪些作物？为了从资助军需供应中获利，布里格斯和其他商人银行家需要一种可以运回欧洲的商品。起初，他们可以依赖埃及的主要出口作物小麦，拿破仑战争期间及之后，马耳他和伊比利亚半岛需要小麦供应英国军队。
然而到 1820 年代，他们需要一种不同的材料来维持商人金融的流动。备选品包括靛蓝、鸦片、丝绸、亚麻籽油（亚麻工业的副产品），以及从苏丹和更南地区运来的阿拉伯胶和象牙等物品。然而这些都不足以资助不断扩大的军火贸易。
en: Financing the expansion of a new power on the Nile created another force needing a diversion through the cotton mills of Lancashire. Muhammad Ali funded the purchase of arms and other warlike materials on credit, which was advanced by these merchants, especially the English firm of Briggs& Co. To obtain the credit, the Pasha offered credit payments of his own, in the form of contracts for the future
delivery of crops.

But which crops? To profit from financing military supplies, Briggs and other merchant bankers needed a commodity they might ship back to Europe. At first, they could rely on Egypt’s main export crop, wheat, which was in demand in Malta and the Iberian Peninsula to supply British forces during and after the Napoleonic wars.

By the 1820s, however, they needed a different material through which to sustain the movement of merchant finance. Alternatives included indigo, opium, silk, linseed oil (a by-product of the linen industry), and items brought from Sudan and further south, such as gum arabic and ivory. None of these, however, was sufficient to finance the expanding trade in arms.

zh: 解决办法由棉花提供。每一部关于埃及及其棉花业的历史都会重复一个故事：一位来自里昂的法国纺织工程师路易·朱梅尔在纽约逗留后抵达埃及，碰巧在开罗一位贵族的花园里“发现”了一种新的长绒棉（即纤维长度较长的棉种），随后说服穆罕默德·阿里广泛种植这种作物，发展出口产业，以满足欧洲纺织制造业的需要。这个故事几乎每一个要素都是神话，由十九世纪法国历史学家和美国外交官编造，他们急于把穆罕默德·阿里治下埃及转型的功劳归于法国或美国。朱梅尔不是里昂人，从未访问美国，受雇于埃及政府是为了发展毛纺厂，而不是棉花产业。他抵达后不到五年就在开罗病逝。
历史学家夸大了他的作用，却忽视了埃及试图从小麦出口国转向棉花出口国的更可能原因。这些原因在于奥斯曼—埃及的扩张，尤其是对苏丹的殖民。
en: The solution was provided by cotton. Every history of Egypt and its cotton industry repeats the story of a French textile engineer from Lyon, Louis Jumel, arriving in Egypt after a stay in New York, who happened to ‘discover’ a new strain of cotton with a long staple, or length of fibre, growing in the garden of a nobleman in Cairo, and who then persuaded Muhammad Ali to plant the crop widely and develop an export industry to serve the needs of European textile manufacturing. Almost every element of this story is a myth, elaborated by nineteenth-century French historians and American diplomats anxious to give France or the United States the credit for the transformation of Egypt under Muhammad Ali. Jumel was not from Lyon, had never visited the United States, and accepted employment from the Egyptian government to develop a woollen factory, not a cotton industry. He became ill and died in Cairo within five years of his arrival.

In exaggerating his role, the historians overlooked the more likely reasons for Egypt’s attempted transformation from an exporter of wheat to an exporter of cotton. Those reasons lay in Ottoman-Egyptian expansion, in particular the colonisation of Sudan.

zh: 如果征服苏丹产生了对武器的需求，它也提供了支付武器的办法。在开罗附近“花园”里种植长绒棉的“贵族”——那无疑是城郊一处有围墙的果园；每个大城镇的富人都会在这样的地方用井水灌溉树木类作物，使其免受尼罗河洪水侵袭——是马胡贝伊·乌尔法利，一位库尔德马穆鲁克，他站在穆罕默德·阿里一边，帮助完成对苏丹的征服，在帕夏的军队中担任高级骑兵军官，后来担任苏丹北部柏柏尔省省长。
通过马胡贝伊，很可能是苏丹——而不是一个法国人——提供了在埃及发展这种作物的模式、动机和棉花品种。
en: If conquering Sudan was the source of a need for arms, it also offered a solution to pay for them. The ‘nobleman’ cultivating long-staple cotton in his ‘garden’ near Cairo – no doubt a walled orchard on the outskirts of the city, a place where the wealthy of every large town used irrigation from wells to grow tree crops protected from the Nile flood – was Mahu Bey al-Urfali, a Kurdish Mamluk who had sided with Muhammad Ali and helped carry out the conquest of Sudan, serving as a senior cavalry officer in the Pasha’s army and then as governor of Berber Province in northern Sudan.
Through Mahu Bey, it was quite probably Sudan, not a Frenchman, that provided the model, the motive, and the cotton variety for the development of the crop in Egypt.

zh: 尼罗河地区发现两种棉花：一种多年生棉花长成小树，短纤维适合粗纱以及床垫和长沙发的填充物；另一种较小，长成灌木，每年用种子重新种植，长绒纤维可纺出用于奢华布料的细线。在埃及，棉花种植很少，因为作为夏季作物，正如我们在
所见，它与田地的夏季泛滥不相容。在南部，棉花仅种在尼罗河沿岸高地；在其他地方，则仅种在有围墙的果园里，那里的灌溉井在夏季供水。
另一方面，在苏丹，尤其是尼罗河的栋古拉和申迪河段，大多数田地高于洪水水位，用水车灌溉，夏季种植十分普遍。
该地区几个世纪以来专门生产棉花，既在河边使用水车，也——至少在近几十年包括破坏性的奥斯曼—埃及征服带来的灾难之前——在井上使用水车，获取由尼罗河补给的地下水。据报道，苏丹的棉纺织厂“为东北非大部分地区提供衣物”。
水车，即萨基亚（
），使用如此广泛，以至于政府收入以对水车的征税而非土地为基础；正如我们在
所指出的，
一词不仅指水车，还指围绕维持每台水车运转所需的家庭、动物和田地组织起来的整个共同体。
en: Two kinds of cotton were found on the Nile, a perennial grown as a small tree, whose short staple was suitable for coarse yarns and as stuffing for mattresses and divans, and a smaller variety, grown as a bush and replanted each year from seed, whose long-staple fibres produced fine threads for luxury cloths. In Egypt, cotton was only sparsely cultivated, since, as a summer crop, it was incompatible, as we saw in
, with the summer inundation of the fields. In the south it was confined to Nile berms and elsewhere to walled orchards, where irrigation wells made water available in summer.

In Sudan, on the other hand, especially on the Dongola and Shendi reaches of the Nile, where most of the fields lay above the flood level and were irrigated with waterwheels, summer cultivation was widely practised.

The region had specialised in cotton production for centuries, using waterwheels both at the river’s edge and, at least before the devastation of recent decades including the destructive Ottoman-Egyptian conquest, on wells accessing groundwater replenished by the Nile. The cotton manufactories of Sudan, it was reported, ‘furnish the greater part of north-eastern Africa with articles of dress’.
The water-wheel, or
, was used so widely that government revenue was based on the taxation of wheels, not land, and the term
referred not just to the wheel, as we noted in
, but to the entire community organised around the households, animals, and fields required to keep each wheel running.

zh: 在殖民苏丹时，穆罕默德·阿里最初的目标是接管这些富裕的农业地区，利用奴隶劳动发展棉花、靛蓝和糖的生产——这种方法在美国南方正被证明是成功的。然而，1822 年苏丹北部的努比亚和阿拉伯语社群反抗占领，杀死了入侵部队的指挥官、穆罕默德·阿里的儿子伊斯梅尔帕夏。土耳其—埃及军队在试图控制上埃及时也遇到了类似的抵抗。
占领者最终镇压了抵抗，并努力发展棉花和靛蓝产业，但他们的主要精力转回了北方。在儿子死去的同一年，穆罕默德·阿里下令在开罗以北的尼罗河三角洲挖掘数千口井并建造水车，大概效仿苏丹模式，以便把种植从灌溉果园扩展到大型田地，实现广泛的夏季种植。
另一家当地商行——布里格斯公司的对手吉巴拉兄弟——为三角洲的新种植园提供信贷。
兰开夏
机械化纺纱的引入，使英国纱厂依赖这些奢侈品种；这不是为了生产更精细的布料，而是因为用较长纤维纺出的纱线在机器过程的粗暴处理中不易被拉断。因此，在利物浦，长绒棉的价格远高于“黎凡特”棉或短绒棉。
en: In colonising Sudan, Muhammad Ali’s initial aim had been to take over these rich agricultural regions and develop cotton, indigo, and sugar production using slave labour – the method that was proving successful in the American South. However, in 1822 the Nubian and Arabic-speaking communities of northern Sudan rebelled against the occupation and killed the commander of the invading forces, Muhammad Ali’s son Isma‘il Pasha. The Turco-Egyptian forces encountered similar opposition to their attempts to control Upper Egypt.

While the occupiers eventually suppressed the resistance and made efforts to develop a cotton and indigo industry, their main efforts moved back to the north. In the same year as the death of his son, Muhammad Ali ordered the digging of thousands of wells and the construction of waterwheels in the Nile Delta north of Cairo, presumably following the Sudanese model, in order to expand cultivation from irrigated gardens into large fields and allow widespread summer cultivation.
Another local merchant firm, the Jibara brothers, rivals of Briggs& Co, supplied credit for a new plantation in the Delta.
The introduction of

mechanised spinning in Lancashire had made British mills dependent on these luxury varieties, not to produce finer cloth but because threads spun from the longer fibres were less liable to pull apart in the rough handling of the machine process. For this reason, in Liverpool long-staple cotton achieved a much higher price than the ‘Levant’ or short-staple variety.

zh: 棉花如今可以为向埃及供应武器提供资金。马胡贝伊把棉花用作获取“优质武器”的手段。
已经为埃及海军供应过船只的塞缪尔·布里格斯，代表穆罕默德·阿里派一艘护卫舰到英格兰，进行包铜处理并安装火炮和其他装备。当费用远远超过该船运去的亚麻籽油货物价值时，布里格斯赊购了工程和武器，然后向利物浦运送了 270 包长绒棉，作为偿还债务的第一期款项。
这批货开启了与兰开夏之间利润丰厚的埃及棉花贸易。在东地中海建造并武装一个强大的新国家，为亚历山大的商人银行家提供了通过曼彻斯特棉纺厂重新引导信用创造的新机会。
en: The cotton could now finance the supply weapons to Egypt. Mahu Bey used the cotton as a means of acquiring ‘weapons of superior quality’.

Samuel Briggs, who had already supplied vessels for the Egyptian navy, sent a frigate to England on behalf of Muhammad Ali, to be coppered and fitted with guns and other equipment. When the expense far exceeded the value of the cargo of linseed oil the ship had carried there, Briggs had the work and the weaponry supplied on credit, then sent a shipment of 270 bales of long-staple cotton to Liverpool, as a first instalment of the repayment of the debt.

This shipment inaugurated a lucrative trade in Egyptian cotton with Lancashire. Building and arming a powerful new state in the Eastern Mediterranean provided the merchant bankers of Alexandria with a new opportunity to reroute credit creation via the cotton mills of Manchester.

zh: 包装贡赋
en: Packaging Tribute

zh: 欧洲的革命战争和奥斯曼帝国的转变，为信用创造突然转向艰难的工厂生产绕道提供了一种解释。这次绕道不是由对商品的简单需求驱动的，而是由对新的信用机制的需要驱动的：战争破坏了旧的商业路线，创造了转移金融票据的迫切需求。然而，欧洲经历的革命和战争——尽管其破坏性超过该大陆近期历史上的任何其他事件——以及尼罗河上新地区强国的建立，都只是更大范围内信用流动及依赖这种流动的利润遭到扰乱的一部分。更广泛的中断不是以欧洲和奥斯曼世界为中心，而是以亚洲殖民政权的转变和美洲以奴隶制为基础的生产体系为中心。
en: The revolutionary wars in Europe and the transformations in the Ottoman Empire offer one explanation for the sudden diversion of credit creation into the difficult detour of factory production. The detour was driven not by a simple demand for goods, but by the need for a new mechanism of credit, when warfare broke up old routes of commerce and created an urgent need for mechanisms to move financial paper. However, the European experience of revolution and war, although more disruptive than any other events in the continent’s recent past, and the building of a new regional power on the Nile were only part of a much wider interruption to the flow of credit, and the profits that depended on it. The broader interruption centred not on Europe and the Ottoman world, but on the transformation of colonial regimes in Asia and the system of slave-based production in the Americas.

zh: 在印度，孟加拉强大商人和信用网络的兴起——这一发展与开罗正在发生的变化相似——削弱了莫卧儿统治，并把英国东印度公司的代理人吸引到从这些商业
网络中获利、在权力斗争中选边站的机会中。
结果，莫卧儿帝国把最富有的领土控制权丢给了公司。1765 年，它被迫授予公司对孟加拉及邻近省份税收的权利。公司从一家军事化贸易公司转变为领土强权。在接下来的几年里，它通过进一步击败欧洲和印度对手扩大了这种权力。因此，正如埃德蒙·伯克所报道的，“商业和统治领域都发生了一场非常重大的革命”。

这一转变虽然确保了公司在印度的财富，却带来了如何把这些收入运回英国的新问题。作为一家贸易公司，其股东和公司职员曾通过为欧洲和印度之间的货物运输融资而致富：运往欧洲的主要是精细纺织品、香料和其他奢侈品。为了通过汇票贴现从贸易融资中获利，公司需要一些东西从欧洲运回印度。由于十七和十八世纪的欧洲几乎不生产任何值得运回亚洲的东西，这种贸易依赖于运送从另一个殖民统治地获取的商品——墨西哥和秘鲁矿山的白银。到 1750 年，白银变得稀缺，于是补充以军需品和海军物资，供针对亚洲和欧洲对手的日益扩大的殖民战争使用，此外还有数量不多的毛织品（通常免运费运输）以及铜和其他金属。
到 1780 年代，船只有时空载驶往印度，运回货物的目的不是互惠贸易，而是包装贡赋，尤其是公司职员作为私人财富获取的那部分。“以货物汇寄贡赋的想法自然使他们对其价格和质量漠不关心——货物本身似乎只是贡赋的一种包装，”伯克解释说，“作为贡赋取得或代替贡赋购买的货物，永远不可能在种类和价格上长期适合一个仅靠商业信誉支撑的市场。”
这种单方面转移贡赋的结果是孟加拉的贫困。但它也导致了伦敦建立在早期互惠商业基础上的票据体系的崩溃。这里谈到的第二种、发生时间更早的中断，是转向制造业的又一个来源。
en: In India, the rise of powerful merchants and credit networks in Bengal, a development similar to the changes under way in Cairo, had weakened Mughal rule and drawn agents of the British East India Company into the opportunities to profit from these commercial
networks and to take sides in the power struggle.

As a result, the Mughal Empire lost control of its richest territories to the Company. In 1765, it had been forced to grant the Company the right to the tax revenues of Bengal and neighbouring provinces. The Company was transformed from a militarised trading corporation into a territorial power. It extended that power over the following years with further defeats of both European and Indian rivals. Consequently, as Edmund Burke reported, ‘a very great revolution took place in commerce as well as in dominion’.

While the transformation secured the riches of the Company in India, it presented the novel problem of how to ship those revenues back to Britain. As a trading firm, its shareholders and company servants had grown rich from financing the movement of goods between Europe and India: mostly fine textiles, spices, and other luxuries to Europe. To profit from the financing of trade, through the discounting of bills of exchange, the Company needed something to ship in the other direction, from Europe back to India. Since Europe in the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries produced almost nothing worth carrying back to Asia, the trade had depended on shipping a commodity sourced in another place of colonial rule, silver from the mines of Mexico and Peru. By 1750, silver was becoming scarce and was supplemented with the shipment of military and naval supplies for the expanding colonial warfare against both Asian and European rivals, along with modest supplies of woollen goods, usually shipped freight-free, and copper and other metals.

By the 1780s, ships were sometimes travelling empty to India, returning with goods whose purpose was not reciprocal trade but a means of packaging tribute, especially the part acquired as private wealth by company servants. ‘The idea of remitting tribute in goods naturally produced an indifference to their price and quality, – the goods themselves appearing little else than a sort of package to the tribute,’ Burke explained. ‘Merchandise taken as tribute, or bought in lieu of it, can never long be of a kind or of a price fitted to a market which stands solely on its commercial reputation.’
