The result of this one-way transfer of tribute was the impoverishment of Bengal. But it also caused the collapse of the paper system in London built on earlier reciprocal commerce. This second and earlier disruption was a further source of the detour into manufacturing.

zh: 第三种扰乱的来源——可以说对信用创造转向制造业最为重要——是由 1775—83 年美国独立战争造成的奴隶贸易和奴隶种植园利润中断，以及大西洋奴隶战争和结束人口贸易的压力对这些
利润构成的更广泛威胁。
美国革命的爆发部分受到印度事件的影响。英国政府曾试图通过授予东印度公司向其北美殖民地运输茶叶的垄断权，来解决印度贸易危机，导致波士顿茶叶商人发起叛乱。北美殖民者试图效仿英国商人移民在印度享有的自由，“强调帝国不同部分——尤其是孟加拉和十三个殖民地——之间的宪制相似性”。
美国人甚至似乎仿用了东印度公司旗帜上的十三道红白条纹，作为新共和国的国旗。
en: The third source of disruption, and, arguably, the most important for the diversion of credit creation into manufacturing, was the interruption to profits from slave trading and slave plantations, caused by the American Revolutionary War of 1775–83 and by wider threats to those
profits from the Atlantic slave war and the pressures to end the trade in humans.

The outbreak of the American Revolution was partly influenced by events in India. The British government had tried to address the crisis in the India trade by awarding the East India Company a monopoly on shipping tea to its North American colonies, causing Boston tea merchants to initiate their rebellion. The North American colonists sought to emulate the freedom enjoyed by British merchant-settlers in India, ‘emphasizing constitutional similarities among the different parts of the empire, especially Bengal and the thirteen colonies’.
The Americans even appear to have copied the thirteen red-and-white stripes of the East India Company ensign for the flag of the new republic.

zh: 但这场叛乱是一场更广泛危机的一部分。奴役非洲人在西印度群岛生产糖、在北美殖民地生产烟草，推动了一个庞大的信用循环。被奴役者在数年或数十年间为其所有者带来回报，因此对他们的奴役不仅产生了人口贸易，还产生了一个不断扩张的信用体系。一个奴隶的价格代表了那些未来劳动年限的资本化价值。
这笔钱通常不是在购买时以现金支付，而是作为债务在数年内偿还给利物浦商人和伦敦代理商人，他们以信用方式为被奴役劳动力的供应提供融资，“主要通过汇票贴现机制”。
汇票贴现也是建立在奴役之上的更广泛三角贸易的主要利润来源。以非洲贸易为例，虽然可以通过商品销售产生收入，但对主导贸易的人来说，主要业务和利润来源是通过汇票贴现组织信用所产生的收入。
大西洋奴隶贸易对整个信用体系的重要性，使它处于“英国政治和经济生活的正中心”。
en: But this rebellion was part of a wider crisis. The enslavement of Africans to work in the production of sugar in the West Indies and tobacco in the North American colonies had given movement to a vast circulation of credit. Enslaved humans generated a return to their owners over years or decades, so their enslavement produced not just a trade in human lives but an expanding system of credit. The price of a slave represented the capitalised value of those prospective years of labour.

It was typically paid not in cash at the moment of purchase, but as a debt repaid over the years to the Liverpool merchants and London commission agents who financed the supply of enslaved labour on credit, ‘mostly through the mechanism of bill discounting’.

The discounting of bills was also a main source of profit in the wider triangular trade built upon enslavement. In the case of the Africa trade, for example, while an income could be generated from merchandise sales, the primary business and source of profit for those who dominated the trade was the income generated from the organising of credit through the discounting of bills.
The importance of the Atlantic slave trade to the entire system of credit positioned it ‘at the very center of English political and economic life’.

zh: 美国革命对这一奴隶金融体系的中断，刺激了棉纺织业的发展。
美国战争使四分之三的伦敦商行破产。在曼彻斯特，五分之四的制造商——其中大多数人既是制造商也是商人——在二十年的战争期间消失了。
前文提到的最早大型棉纺厂之一奎里班克纱厂，就是在奴隶贸易受扰、北美贸易中断之后建立的，而拥有该厂的格雷格家族主要从事的正是这些贸易，他们拥有奴隶种植园和商船
运输业务。
与受法国战争打乱的德国商人一样，活跃于大西洋贸易的人积累了大量汇票，以及通过赊售被奴役者、或从因战争被迫破产的所有者手中收购加勒比奴隶种植园而获得的债券。兰开夏与加勒比奴隶制的密切联系，使英格兰这个地区在货币意义上独一无二。作为大西洋体系的一部分，它是全国唯一一个汇票而非硬币、地方银行券或其他信用形式充当主要货币来源的地区。
大西洋体系形成了密集的信用货币网络，却被战时封锁和中断打乱。棉花生产提供了一种疏通这些流动的手段，尤其是因为它促进了“第二次奴隶制”的发展，即把被奴役者大规模重新部署到美国南方的新种植区，而种族灭绝和生态毁灭为扩张清除了道路。
作为另一个半球的收成，棉花受到长途运输不确定性和遥远气候不可预测性的影响，为投机性贸易和保险合同创造了更多获利机会。
棉花还具有一种不同寻常的商品特性：它可以双向运输，先作为原棉运往兰开夏，然后作为制成品返回美洲。在其他时候，原料生产者会避免这种迂回过程，把制造过程搬到棉花原本的产地——那里同时也是制成品后来的销售地。但在这个案例中，生产者是被奴役的，种植园主可以阻止他们自己织布，因为种植园主的利润需要这种运输绕道。
从汇票中获利，依赖于这种组织绕道、创造信用货币双向流动的能力。
en: The interruption to this system of slave finance from the American Revolution was a spur to the development of cotton manufacturing.

The American war bankrupted three-quarters of the London merchant houses. In Manchester, four out of five manufacturers, most of them merchants as much as manufacturers, disappeared during the two decades of war.

Quarry Bank Mill, already mentioned as one of the first large cotton mills, was set up after disruptions to the slave trade and interruptions to the North American trade in which the proprietors, the Greg family, owners of slave plantations and merchant
shipping, were mainly involved.

Like the German merchants disrupted by the French wars, those active in the Atlantic trade accumulated large numbers of bills of exchange, as well as the bonds acquired in the credit sale of enslaved people or in the acquisition of Caribbean slave plantations from owners forced into bankruptcy by the war. The close connections between Lancashire and Caribbean slavery made that region of England unique in monetary terms. As an element of the Atlantic system, it was the one part of the country in which bills of exchange, rather than specie, local banknotes, or other forms of credit, functioned as the main source of money.

Forming a dense network of credit money, the Atlantic system was thrown into disarray by the wartime blockages and interruption. Cotton production provided a means to unblock these flows, not least because it facilitated the development of ‘the second slavery’, the vast redeployment of enslaved people to the new plantation zones of the American South, where genocide and ecocide cleared the path of expansion.

As the harvest of another hemisphere, cotton was subject to the uncertainty of longdistance shipping and the unpredictability of a distant climate, creating additional opportunities for profit from both speculative trading and insurance contracts.

Cotton also had the unusual character of a commodity that could be shipped in both directions, first as raw cotton to Lancashire and then as manufactured products crossing back to the Americas. In other times, the producers of the raw material would have avoided this circuitous process by bringing the manufacturing process to where the cotton was first produced and later sold as a finished product. But, in this case, the producers, being enslaved, could be prevented from making their own cloth by the owners of the plantations, whose profit required the detour of shipping.
Profiting from bills of exchange depended on this ability to organise a detour, creating reciprocal movements of credit money.

zh: 把现代工业生活的兴起视为一次历史绕道，有几个好处。第一，它有助于避开技术决定论问题——这一问题在殖民灌溉史、优步的故事以及许多其他领域中已经遇到过，在这些领域中，技术被视为一种自行推动改进的力量。第二，它避免把西北欧一小块地方、以及该地域内一个更小地区兰开夏历史上的“例外性断裂”变成一种范式，用来解释世界每个角落工业化的成败或“发展”的成败。
第三，它用一种从未来攫取方式、即资本化来理解资本的路径，取代生产主义的资本主义理解，后者不可避免地
以工业生产的故事为中心。
en: To approach the rise of modern industrial life as a historical detour has several advantages. First, it helps avoid the issue of technical determinism, a problem already encountered in the history of colonial irrigation, the story of Uber, and many other areas, where technology is taken to be a self-moving force of improvement. Second, it avoids turning an ‘exceptional discontinuity’ in the history of a small corner of northwest Europe, and of an even smaller region within that territory, Lancashire, into a paradigm that can explain the success and failure of industrialisation or ‘development’ in every corner of the world.
Third, it replaces a productivist understanding of capitalism, which inevitably
centres on the story of industrial production, with an approach that understands capital in terms of modes of capture of the future, or capitalisation.

zh: 这种路径并不要求低估英国所发生之事后来的重要性。但它可以从临界点的角度来界定这种重要性。绕道和中断可能偶然启动新的过程，产生广泛影响。
其中之一就是雇佣劳动所促成的信用生产转变，我们现在就来讨论这一点。
en: This approach does not require minimising the subsequent significance of what happened in Britain. But it can frame that significance in terms of tipping points. Detours and disruptions can accidentally set in motion new processes, with wide repercussions.
One of those is the transformation in credit production enabled by wage labour, to which we now turn.

zh: 恶是小额货币之根
en: Evil Is the Root of Small Money

zh: 我们现在可以讨论对生产主义、技术驱动、欧洲中心的资本史或资本化史论的第二个修正。工业革命是一次绕道。它提供了一条新的循环回路，一种把从债务创造中获利的机会折向不同路径、扩大攫取装置的办法。但它做到这一点，不仅是通过建立需要融资的新路线和新商品。它还附带创造了一套庞大的新信用机器：大批工人被组织进工厂和煤矿，领取货币工资。
en: We can now consider the second modification to productivist, technology-driven, European-centred arguments about the history of capital, or capitalisation. The industrial revolution was a detour. It offered a new circuit, a way of bending onto a different path the opportunities for profiting from the creation of debt, amplifying the apparatuses of capture. But it did this not only through establishing new routes and goods to be financed. It incidentally created an extensive new machinery of credit: large bodies of workers, organised into factories and coal mines, who were to be paid a monetary wage.

zh: 雇佣劳动常被视为现代工业资本主义的一个决定性特征，尤其是工厂生产中受纪律约束、受时间管理的劳动。工资把人类行动者分为提供劳动者和拥有资本者，把制造业及其他生产的产品分为付给雇员的工资和资本所有者索取的利息与利润。一方面是小时工资或月工资，另一方面是利息和利润，这种对比似乎使工人劳动所得与资本非劳动所得之间非同寻常的差异显得正常。对于莫伊舍·波斯通——上一代最有影响力的马克思理论重新阐释者之一——来说，工资对于“价值”效果至关重要，资本主义下的社会支配正是通过这种效果组织起来的。波斯通认为，即使承认生产过程产生的剩余并非全都是劳动的产物——这不同于较早的马克思主义研究，而恰恰在承认这一点时尤其如此——工资仍然发挥着强大的功能。它以统一的时间增量衡量劳动价值，从而使一切劳动变得可比。这种
过程把所有生产性工作转化为同一种
看似抽象的活动的单位。小时和分钟的同质、空洞的统一性——按既定费率支付，并表现为该劳动的“价格”——作为一种支配性抽象运作，创造出一种支配模式：把越来越大份额的收益分配给不为此工作的人。
en: Wage labour is often seen as a defining feature of modern, industrial capitalism, especially the disciplined, time-managed labour of factory production. The wage separates human agents into those who provide labour and those who own capital, dividing the product of manufacturing and other production into wages paid to employees and the interest and profit claimed by owners of capital. The contrast between an hourly or monthly wage, on the one hand, and interest and profit, on the other, appears to normalise the extraordinary difference between the earned income of the worker and the unearned income of capital. For Moishe Postone – among the most influential reinterpreters of Marxian theory of the last generation – the wage is central to the effect of ‘value’ through which social domination under capitalism is organised. Even if one acknowledges, unlike older Marxian scholarship, that not all of the surplus generated by processes of production is a product of labour, indeed especially with that acknowledgement, Postone argues, the wage still performs a powerful function. It makes all labour comparable, by measuring its value in uniform increments of time. This process of
transforms all productive work into units of the same

seemingly abstract activity. The homogeneous, empty uniformity of hours and minutes of labour, paid at a given rate and appearing as the ‘price’ of that labour, operates as a governing abstraction, creating the mode of domination that allocates a larger and increasing share of earnings to those who do not work for them.

zh: 这一分析虽然有说服力，却忽略了一点。工资作为一种抽象而运作，不仅在于：对许多工人而言，工资的“价值”是用抽象的小时和分钟来表示的。它以另一种或许更有效的方式抽象。与以小时和分钟计算价值的装置一样，这种效果依赖于对时间的部署。然而，它不是工厂雇佣那种一丝不苟的“时间纪律”，尽管那可能很重要。它是那种不精确、未经计量、由来已久的推迟和延迟机制——只是以新的规模实行。与从生产性劳动中获利的较早形式一样，延迟采取的形式是工作履行与工资支付之间的时间间隔，尤其是工资支付与其用于消费支出之间的间隔。这样看待工资，不是把焦点从生产领域转向交换和消费领域——这些区分在今天越来越没有意义——而是理解工资作为信用生产装置的意义。
我们将看到，工资以信用货币支付。从中获得的利润是
进入制造业的意外后果。这一后果的表现和持续时间都将超过制造业本身的优势。
en: This analysis, for all its persuasiveness, overlooks something. The wage operates as an abstraction not only through the abstractness of the hours and minutes in which, for many workers, its ‘value’ is presented. It abstracts in another, perhaps more effective way. Like the device of calculating value in hours and minutes, this effect rests on the deployment of time. However, it is not the meticulous ‘time discipline’ of factory employment, significant as that may be. It is the inexact, unmeasured, age-old mechanism of postponement and delay – practised on a new scale. As with older forms of profiting from productive labour, the delay takes the form of the gap in time between the performance of work and its payment, and, even more so, between the paying of the wage and its spending on consumption. To see the wage in this way is not to shift focus from the sphere of production to that of exchange and consumption – distinctions that make less and less sense today – but, rather, to understand the significance of the wage as a device for the production of credit.
The wage was paid in credit money, as we will see. The profit to be made from it was an unanticipated consequence of the
into manufacturing. It was a consequence that would outperform and outlast the advantages of manufacturing itself.

zh: 什么是工资，又如何支付？工厂的不同寻常之处，在于把几十名、有时几百名工人置于一家企业的控制之下。这产生了一个问题：在一个主要依靠账面信用组织起来、家庭仆人和许多其他工作人员大多以食物和衣物支付报酬的世界里，如何找到给他们发钱的手段？
习惯于只在特殊情况下使用硬币、或只在账簿无法“结算”或无法用更多信用来对账时结清年度账目的商人，突然需要一种每周或每月末进行大量小额支付的手段。许多货币史研究把这描述为一场危机，导致人们反复努力寻找某种得到广泛使用的“小额货币”形式。
然而，我们可以不把这视为工业扩张的障碍，而视为工业扩张所创造的机会。事实上，它可能是理解这种扩张的关键。当代经济
理论中一个有影响的论点提出，对货币的需要源于交换行为参与者之间缺乏信任，因此“恶是一切货币之根”。
或许更好的看法是，以工厂劳动剥削条件为形态的恶，是
货币之根：如今突然需要用来支付工资的硬币、代金券和纸币。这些轻小的象征物——以
形式存在的货币——很快就会被人误认为货币的一般本质。
en: What was a wage, and how was it paid? The factory was unusual in bringing under the control of one firm dozens and, in some cases, hundreds of workers. This produced a problem: how to find the money to pay them, in communities organised largely on the use of book credit, in a world where domestic servants and many other kinds of staff were paid mostly in food and clothing.

Merchants accustomed to using coinage only in exceptional circumstances, or to settle yearly accounts when the books could not be ‘reckoned’, or reconciled, with further credits, suddenly needed a means of making large numbers of small payments at the end of every week or month. Many studies of monetary history portray this as a crisis, leading to repeated efforts to find a means of introducing some widely used form of ‘small money’.

However, we can see this not as an obstacle to the expansion of industrial production but as the opportunity it created. In fact, it may be a key to understanding that expansion. An influential argument in contemporary economic
theory proposes that the need for money arises from the lack of trust between those involved in an act of exchange, and thus that ‘evil is the root of all money’.
It may be better to see evil, in the shape of the exploitative conditions of factory labour, as the root of
money: the coins, chits, and banknotes now suddenly required for paying wages. These slight, token things – money in the form of
– would soon come to be mistaken for the nature of money in general.

zh: 以前，大商人往往不仅参与获取货物，还参与为货物生产融资，办法是一种被称为外放制的信用操作：商人把材料借贷给农民、织工或布商。

以支付工资为基础的工厂生产强化了这种控制，但也代表了一种从信用创造中获利的新方法。在外放制中，无论农业还是手工业，商人通常借出种子、羊毛、亚麻或其他必需品，而耕作者或织工借出自己的劳动。商人以折扣价提前“购买”成品，生产者则用产品全额偿还预付款。由此产生的产品为这些贷款带来利润。商人和工人之间的利润分配反映了他们力量的不平等。在工厂生产中，工人如今向厂主提供信用。他们工作一整天或一整周，把自己的劳动借给雇主。这笔贷款产生剩余，即所付劳动工资与该劳动产品价值之间的差额，这笔剩余由雇主获得。
en: Previously, large merchants had often been involved not only in procuring goods but in financing their production, through the credit operation known as the putting-out system, where merchants loaned materials to a farmer, weaver, or clothier.

Factory production, based on the payment of a wage, intensified this control, but also represented a new method to profit from credit creation. In putting out, both in farming and in handicraft, the merchant typically loaned the seed, wool, flax, or other requirements, while the cultivators or weavers loaned their labour. The merchant paid a discounted price to ‘purchase’ in advance the finished product, while the producer repaid the advance in full with the product. The resulting product yielded a profit on these loans. The share of profit going to merchant and worker reflected their unequal strength. With factory production, the workers now advanced credit to the mill owner. They worked an entire day or week, loaning their labour to the employer. This loan yielded a surplus, the difference between the wage paid for the labour and the value of the product of that labour, a surplus that was acquired by the employer.

zh: 商品和服务生产中大规模组织劳动，如何成为另一种攫取装置？

现代商业银行的货币创造能力，最初是通过为对外贸易、战争和奴役提供融资发展起来的。正是通过那些特殊的装置，货币被“物质化”，从单纯的记账单位转变为对未来付款的具体索取权——变成“真正的”货币。然而，当工业生产把一种国内的工资支付制度普遍化时，货币可以通过第二种方式物质化，即通过国内的劳动过程。就连日常的商品制造过程，也可以成为攫取未来的装置。棉纺织业特别适合这一角色：作为世界商业的“怪胎”，它以奴隶种植园和工厂中的劳动资本化为基础，使通过信用攫取剩余的机会翻倍。
en: How does the large-scale organisation of labour in the production of goods and services become another apparatus of capture?

Modern commercial banking developed its powers of money creation initially through the financing of foreign trade, warfare, and enslavement. It was through those exceptional apparatuses that money was ‘materialised’, transformed from a mere unit of account into a concrete claim on future payments – into ‘real’ money. However, when industrial production generalised a domestic regime of wage payment, money could be materialised in a second way, through the labour process at home. Even the daily process of making goods could become an apparatus for the capture of the future. Cotton manufacturing was particularly suited to this role: as a ‘freak’ of world commerce, based on the capitalisation of labour both on slave plantations and in factories, it doubled the opportunities for the capture of surplus through credit.

zh: 大规模雇佣的组织通常被理解为通过支付工资“购买”劳动。但这种

市场交换的形象是一种虚构——尽管不是通常所解释的那种虚构方式。雇主或企业通常不用过去积累的资金支付工人。工人以信用货币获得报酬：他们的工资是一笔贷款。起初，信用体系的运作相当明显。例如，1820 年代的英格兰，约克郡纺织织造商约翰·福斯特父子公司在工人劳动一个月后才“支付”工资，而且不是用现金，而是给每个织工的账户记一笔信用。与此同时，公司向雇员供应货物，包括“煤、蜡烛、布匹、面粉、麦芽、牛奶、糖、糖浆和奶酪”，使他们持续负债。工资只是从这些长期债务中扣除。其他公司直接用“实物”或物质商品支付工人。truck（实物支付）一词最初意味着用一种物品交换另一种物品，但实物支付并不是物物交换安排。工资被记为账面信用，预支给工人，用于购买雇主供应的货物。这些货物通常定价过高，有时只是未售出的纺织品或企业的其他产品。或者，工人得到代金券、代币或纸币，只能在公司自营商店兑现。
en: The organisation of large-scale employment is usually understood as the ‘purchase’ of labour, via the payment of a wage. But that image of a

market exchange is a fiction – although not in the way the fiction is usually explained. The employer or firm does not typically pay workers with funds accumulated from the past. The workers are paid in credit money: their wage is a loan. Initially, the working of the credit system was quite visible. In England in the 1820s, for example, the Yorkshire textile-weaving firm of John Foster and Sons ‘paid’ its workers one month in arrears, and not in cash but by assigning a credit to each weaver’s account. Meanwhile, the firm supplied its employees with goods, including ‘coal, candles, cloth, flour, malt, milk, sugar, treacle and cheese’, leaving them continuously in debt. The wage was simply a deduction from these standing debts. Other firms paid their workers directly in ‘truck’, or material goods. The term trucking originally implied giving or trafficking one item in exchange for another, but payments in truck were not barter arrangements. The wage was recorded as book credit, advanced to the worker, to be spent on goods supplied by the employer. The goods were typically overpriced, and sometimes consisted of just unsold textiles or other produce of the business. Or the workers were paid in vouchers, tokens, or notes that were redeemable only at the company-owned shop.

zh: 1806 年，曼彻斯特商人塞缪尔·希伯特匿名出版了一本小册子，论述使用“小面额纸币”的弊端。这种做法的出现，源于制造商发行期票
en: In 1806, Samuel Hibbert, a Manchester merchant, published anonymously a pamphlet on the evil of the use of ‘small notes’. Their use had arisen from the practice of manufacturers issuing promissory notes

zh: 以支付其雇工；本来每周都必须筹措一笔现金来支付这些雇工；如果用这种方便的纸片就能满足他们，那么应付给他们的工资——随着时间推移必然达到相当可观的数额——就可以由雇主用于贸易。这种流通还因如下想法而受到进一步鼓励：对于由此获得的信用，他们不必支付任何利息。
en: to pay persons in their service, for whom a quantity of cash must be procured each week; and if they can be satisfied with such convenient paper, the wages due to them, which in the course of time, must amount to a very considerable sum, can be used by their employers in trade. Such a circulation is still farther encouraged, by the reflection, that for credit thus obtained, they pay no interest.

zh: 换言之，正如殖民商人与其说从货物供应中获利，不如说从信用创造中获利，而种植园奴隶制和货物供应是这种信用创造的机制；同样，新兴的大型纺织制造商——其中多数人起家于长途贸易商人——发现制造业的剩余不必来自机械化生产日益提高的效率。技术效率永远不可能成为长期差别利润的来源，即使像让—巴蒂斯特·萨伊或他兄弟糖业公司所经历的那种故障、挫折和事故被克服，因为竞争对手公司很快就会达到
同样的效率。
更可靠的剩余来源，可以是新信用体系的规模——在这个体系中，工人的工资不是以现金支付，而是以雇主的期票或账面信用支付。
en: In other words, just as colonial merchants made their profit not so much from the supply of goods, but from the creation of credit for which plantation slavery and the supply of goods was the mechanism, in the same way the emergent large textile manufacturers, most of whom began as long-distance merchants, discovered that the surplus from manufacturing did not have to arise from the increasing efficiency of mechanised production. Technical efficiency could never be a longterm source of differential profit, even once the breakdowns, setbacks, and accidents experienced by men like Jean-Baptiste Say or his brother’s sugar company were overcome, as rival firms would soon adopt the
same efficiencies.
Surplus could arise more reliably from the scale of the new system of credit, in which the wages of workers were paid not in cash, but in the employer’s promissory notes or book credit.

zh: 议会曾多次试图取缔实物支付的做法，1831 年的《实物工资法》在许多行业中禁止这种做法，1887 年又将禁令扩大到更多领域。1831 年的立法是《工厂法》的前身；《工厂法》代表着规范工资及其与工时关系的更广泛尝试，帮助确立了一种印象：工资是时间与劳动的直接交换，而不是信用体系的一个方面——在这个体系中，雇主实际上攫取了贷款利息。但甚至在实物支付被取缔之前，用来支付工资的信用货币创造就已经变得如此普遍，以至于它不再表现为贷款，也不再依赖个别雇主发行自己的票据或代币。
en: Parliament attempted repeatedly to outlaw the practice of truck payment, banning it in many trades in the Truck Act of 1831, and extending the ban more widely in 1887. The 1831 legislation was a precursor to the Factory Acts, which represented a wider attempt to regulate wages and their relation to hours of work, helping to establish the impression that the wage was a direct exchange of time for labour rather than the aspect of a credit system in which the employer in effect captured the interest on a loan. But even before truck payments were outlawed, the creation of credit money to pay wages had become so general that it no longer appeared as a loan, and no longer depended on individual employers issuing their own notes or tokens.
body.review: 校注：底本此处确作“时间与劳动的直接交换”（a direct exchange of time for labour），与本章其他地方的工资与劳动交换表述有异。译文照录，未擅自将time改为money。

zh: 在英格兰，随着十八世纪末和十九世纪初制造业的发展，涌现出数百家小银行，通常由当地商人和商人兼制造商创办。
它们的信用创造能力最初是通过为贸易融资发展起来的，如今可以在雇佣劳动这一新领域扩展，这需要银行发行面额更小但数量更大的纸币。“在地方上，小面额纸币成为支付工资的常见方式，到 1825 年，许多地区银行家发行量的一半或更多是面额低于 5 英镑的纸币。”
随着催生现代工业的更广泛商人信用和银行体系的发展，商人或银行会通过创造信用货币来预支支付工资的钱。工人用这些信用购买自己和他人生产的商品。这些购买是把资金返还银行体系、偿还信用创造所依凭之贷款的手段。这些购买代表了工人所生产之物的全部价值，因为信用货币只能相对于它将据以收回的未来产品和服务而被创造出来。
与实物工资制一样，利润是通过这个信用装置“攫取”的：制造商和零售商对货物的定价高于其生产成本。
en: In England, hundreds of small banks emerged with the development of manufacturing in the late eighteenth and early nineteenth century, typically formed by local merchants or merchant manufacturers.

Their power of credit creation, initially developed through financing trade, could be expanded in the new field of wage labour, requiring the issuing of paper notes by the banks in smaller denominations, but in larger quantities. ‘In the provinces small notes became the common method of paying wages, and by 1825 one-half or more of the issues of the bankers in many districts were notes of less than £5.’

As the wider system of merchant credit and banking that spawned modern industry developed, merchants or banks would advance the money for wages, by the creation of credit money. Workers spent these credits on the goods that they and others produced. These purchases were the means of returning the funds to the banking system, in repayment of the loan through which the credit had been created. The purchases represented the entire value of what the workers produced, for credit money can be created only in relation to the future products and services through which it will be recaptured.
As with the system of truck, profit was ‘captured’ through this credit apparatus, by the manufacturer and retailer charging more for the goods than the cost of their production.

zh: 为了使这套体系普遍化，信用创造逐渐由一个独特的实体——银行——来管理，银行逐渐从最初兼营贸易、信用创造和生产安排的商人商行中分离出来。银行发行的信用货币被标准化为支付工人“工资”的手段。银行发行纸币的做法逐渐统一。最终，只有
一种纸币，即中央银行或财政部的纸币——在此即英格兰银行的纸币——被使用。货币取代了商人、雇主和地方银行发行的多种货币，呈现出统一的全国性制度的外观。
然而，尽管政府逐渐垄断了纸币印刷，正如它们先前垄断了硬币铸造，私人商业银行仍保留着创造货币的权力。几乎所有货币仍然是通过私人创造的：银行为企业和个人客户开立账户，客户开具支票或安排付款，使这种信用货币在企业之间或从雇主向工人转移。大型企业——尤其在美国——也在货币创造中发挥作用，不仅通过发行股票和债券，还通过创造商业票据；美国大型企业广泛使用商业票据支付工资。
en: To generalise this system, the creation of credit came to be managed by a distinct entity, the banking house, which gradually separated itself from the merchant houses that had originally combined trade, credit creation, and the arranging of production. The credit money issued by banks was standardised as a means of payment of a worker’s ‘wage’. The issuing of notes by banks was gradually made uniform. Eventually, only

one note, that of the central bank or treasury – in this case, the Bank of England – was used. In place of multiple kinds of money issued by merchants, employers, and local banks, money took on the appearance of a uniform, national institution.

However, while governments came to monopolise the printing of paper money, just as they had earlier monopolised the minting of coins, private commercial banks retained their power to create money. Almost all money continued to be privately created, through banks opening accounts for business and individual customers, who wrote cheques or arranged payments that transferred this credit money between firms or from employers to workers. Large enterprises, especially in the United States, also played a role in money creation, not only through issuing shares and bonds, but through the creation of commercial paper, widely used by large firms in the United States to pay wages.

zh: 这种创造信用货币以支付工资的安排，确认了“抽象劳动”的效果，即一种印象：工人只是在参与交换行为，用其劳动的使用权换取标准化的“货币”支付。从这个角度看，工业革命代表着信用关系的扩展和重组，而不是从商业资本向产业资本的转变。
en: This arrangement of creating credit money to pay wages confirmed the effect of ‘abstract labour’, the impression that workers were simply involved in an act of exchange, trading the use of their labour for a standardised payment in ‘money’. From this perspective, the industrial revolution represented an extension and reorganisation of credit relations, rather than a shift from commercial capital to industrial capital.

zh: 城市与商业
en: City Business

zh: 还有另一种方式可以让我们把工业化视为某种绕道。另外两种机制很快就将超越并取代工厂，成为组织未来资本化的主要场所。与工厂一样，它们各自提供了一种攫取装置，把未来收入转化为当下可以折扣价获得的资产；它们也各自提供了一种安排或场所，用来组织关于货币和物质生活的知识。其中之一后来被称为“商业”，另一种被称为城市生活或“城市”。商业和城市都不是用来理解物质过程的新对象。但在十九世纪后期和二十世纪初，无论是在欧洲还是在殖民世界的许多地方，二者都成为值得关注的事项，很像几十年前的“工业”，因为它们各自成为扩张性新攫取权力的焦点。考察它们的出现，将有助于我们重新定位工业生产的地位——并理解后来向“经济”观念的转向，这个问题将在接下来的章节中探讨。
en: There is a further way in which we can see industrialisation as something of a detour. Two other mechanisms were soon to overtake and displace the factory as principal sites of organising the capitalisation of the future. Like the factory, each of these provided an apparatus of capture that transformed future revenue into assets that could be acquired at a discount in the present; each also provided an arrangement or site for organising knowledge about money and material life. One of these came to be known as ‘business’, the other as urban life or ‘the city’. Neither business nor the city was a new object for making sense of material processes. But, in the later nineteenth and early twentieth century, both in Europe and in many parts of the colonised world, each emerged as a matter of concern, much like ‘industry’ in earlier decades, as each became the focus of expansive new powers of capture. Looking at their emergence will help us resituate the significance of industrial production – and to understand the later turn to the idea of ‘the economy’, a question to be explored in the chapters that follow.

zh: 十九世纪的资本家似乎很少乐意通过工业过程来攫取收入。制造业既费力又常常危险，即使对厂主来说也是如此。让—巴蒂斯特·萨伊因为机器故障造成的困难而放弃制造业，这并不例外。欧内斯特·克罗尼耶在一次工业事故中失去一根手指——此人后来把萨伊家族的炼糖帝国变成投机贸易生意，并使其破产——则是又一个提醒。
约克郡的商人兼制造商威廉·布鲁克被热靛蓝染料溅到而失明后，把纱厂的管理权交给儿子们，自己转而投资铁路股票。

格雷格家族的纱厂已经成为英国最大的纺织制造商，却发现自己几乎无利可图，部分原因是父亲把公司传给四个儿子后，仍就建筑和机器的最初成本收取租金，从不折旧。儿子们很快厌倦了这种辛苦，甚至连罗伯特也是如此，他经营的是贸易和融资业务，而不是纱厂本身。“我会发现我在买好棉花、卖好价和融好资上花费的时间、注意力和焦虑都毫无回报，”他向父亲抱怨道。另一个儿子则想知道还要过多久“在这里过这种狗一样的生活。我从不打开一本书……早上五点半起床，晚上十点上床，整天像划桨奴隶一样劳作”。
和父亲一样，也像大多数商人一样，儿子们对成为食租者的兴趣，甚至超过了对没有回报的制造业的兴趣。
公司通过收购其他纱厂而扩张，部分是以接收纱厂来抵偿别人因利润更高的棉花贸易业务而欠他们的债务，但也因为他们能以 3.25% 的利率抵押纱厂借入资金，然后用借来的资金投机，赚取 5% 的收益。最终，无论是奎里班克纱厂还是他们拥有的其他任何纱厂——那些气势恢宏、标志性的工业革命场所——都不再靠制造业赚钱。
en: Nineteenth-century capitalists seldom seemed to enjoy having to capture revenue through the industrial process. Manufacturing was laborious and often dangerous, even for the mill owners. Jean-Baptiste Say was not exceptional in abandoning manufacturing due to the difficulties caused by the breakdown of machinery. The finger lost in an industrial accident by Ernest Cronier, the man who then turned the Say family’s sugar-refining empire into a speculative trading business, and bankrupted it, was another reminder.

William Brooke, a merchant-manufacturer in Yorkshire, handed the management of his yarn-making mill to his sons after becoming blind from being splashed with hot indigo, and invested instead in railway shares.

The Greg family, whose mills had become the largest textile manufacturer in Britain, found themselves making little or no profit, in part because the father, having passed the firm onto his four sons, continued to claim a rent on the initial cost of the buildings and machinery, never depreciating their value. The sons soon tired of the effort, even Robert, who ran the trading and financing operations rather than the mills themselves. ‘I shall find I have given my time, attention and anxiety in buying cotton well, selling well and financing well, for nothing,’ he complained to his father. Another son wondered how long ‘to continue the dog’s life I am leading here. I never open a book . . . rise at 5:30 a.m., go to bed at 10 p.m. and toil like a galley-slave all day’.
Like the father, and like most business people, even the sons were more interested in becoming rentiers than the unrewarding work of manufacturing.

The company expanded through acquiring other mills, partly in settlement of debts owed from the more lucrative cotton-trading operations, but also because they could borrow funds at 3.25 per cent mortgaged on the mills, then earn 5 per cent by speculating with the borrowed funds. Eventually, neither Quarry Bank nor any of their other mills, those imposing, iconic sites of the industrial revolution, was making money from manufacturing.

zh: 格雷格家族、萨伊炼糖公司以及许多其他人的经历，代表了一种更大的变化。几十年内，制造业已被另一种转变超越，即“商业”的兴起。这是十九世纪后期出现的一个术语，用来命名一种新现象：现代股份公司和它的新伙伴机构投资银行同时发展起来。
en: The experience of the Greg family, the Say refinery company, and many others typifies a larger change. Within a few decades, manufacturing had been overtaken by another transformation, the rise of ‘business’. This was the term that emerged in the later nineteenth century to name a new phenomenon, the simultaneous development of the modern joint-stock company and its new partner institution, the investment bank.

zh: 正如
所指出的，从 1860 年代到 1914 年的半个世纪，以两项相互关联的发展为标志。在第一次世界大战前的两
代人的时间里，北半球少数几个强国巩固了对全球南方大多数国家以及北美现存原住民的帝国统治。
与此同时，这个时代以新规模的改造地球工程为特征：长途铁路、大型船运运河和海港、跨洋电报、城市照明和电力发展，以及河流系统的重新工程化。同样，它也以帝国权力和技术项目的新规模所促成的债务创造新形式为特征。
en: As noted in
, the half-century from the 1860s to 1914 was marked by two interconnected developments. Within the space of two

generations before the First World War, a handful of powers in the northern hemisphere consolidated imperial rule over most countries of the Global South, as well as the surviving native peoples of North America.

At the same time, it was an era defined by terraforming projects on a new scale: long-distance railways, large ship canals and sea ports, trans-oceanic telegraphs, the development of municipal lighting and electric power, and the re-engineering of river systems. Equally, it was defined by the novel forms of debt creation that the new scale of imperial power and technical projects enabled.

zh: 帝国的批评者用新术语“帝国主义”来描述由金融驱动的支配扩张。
许多批评者逐渐把这种金融扩张及其输出海外视为一种“过剩”资本的流动，这种剩余是由“资本在已进入机器经济的制造业中拥塞”以及低工资造成的剩余“储蓄”所创造的。
这种观点反映了我们在此考察过的对货币的同样误解。金融资本在很大程度上，并不是由现有企业的剩余或储蓄经银行或私人投资者转投新项目而形成的。它是金融业制造的信用货币，是一种把未来收入在当下资本化的手段。它的创造不取决于是否有过去积累的剩余可供吸收，而取决于能否把未来建构为一种对尚待获取的剩余的可靠索取权，使这种索取权能够在当下变现和交易。
en: Critics of empire described the finance-driven expansion of domination with the new term ‘imperialism’.

Many of the critics came to see this expansion of finance and its export abroad as the flow of an ‘excess’ of capital, a surplus created by the ‘congestion of capital in the manufacturing industries which have entered the machine economy’ and the ‘saving up’ of surplus because of low wages.

This view reflects the same misunderstanding of money we have examined here. Finance capital, for the most part, does not come into being as the surplus or savings from existing business, redirected through banks or private investors into new ventures. It is credit money, manufactured by the industry of finance, as a means of capitalising in the present a future revenue. Its creation depends not on the availability of a surplus to absorb from the past, but on the construction of a future in the form of a reliable claim on a surplus to be acquired, in a manner that can be realised and traded in the present.

zh: 因此，十九世纪后期信用机制的这次扩张不应被理解为一种与先前工业扩张相对的“金融”扩张，而应理解为一种技术政治扩张。信用的创造不仅需要日益增多的金融家、投资银行家和股票推销商的努力。它需要技术设备和改造地球，从而通过一种机制制造和控制未来收入流；这种机制在可靠性、产权、帝国扩张和暴力执行方面的形式，使这些收入流在当下可得。这些安排补充了管理未来收入的较早装置——无论是通过殖民贸易、奴隶种植园和政府发动战争，还是甚至通过煤矿开采和制造业的绕道——在大多数情况下最终超越了它们。
en: This later-nineteenth-century expansion of credit mechanisms should therefore be understood not as a ‘financial’ expansion, in contrast to the industrial expansion that preceded it, but as a technopolitical one. The creation of credit required not just the efforts of a proliferating class of financiers, investment bankers, and stock promoters. It required the technical equipment and terraforming through which future flows of revenue could be manufactured and controlled via a mechanism whose forms of reliability, property, imperial expansion, and violent enforcement made them available in the present. These arrangements supplemented the older apparatuses for governing future revenue, whether through colonial trade, slave plantations, and government war-making, or even the detour of coal mining and manufacturing, in most cases eventually overtaking them.

zh: 正如我们所见，1860 年代至 1914 年期间的技术和科学发展具有一组相互关联的特征，它们促进了这种新的收入攫取，同时又
受到这种攫取的鼓励——技术与物质耐久性的新形式，伴随着法律和经济学的变化，为建造收入攫取装置提供了新方法。这些还涉及货币创造的新方法。
en: As we saw, the technical and scientific developments of the period from the 1860s to 1914 had a set of interrelated characteristics that facilitated this new capture of revenue and were simultaneously

encouraged by it – the new forms of technical and material durability, accompanied by changes in law and economics, allowing new ways to build apparatuses for the capture of revenue. These also involved new methods of money creation.

zh: 作为一台代际财富转移的机器，股份公司需要另一个组织——投资银行——的协助。投资银行不同于较早的商人银行，后者为殖民贸易和动产奴隶制提供融资，并创造那些活动所依赖的新规模战争所需的政府债务。它们也不同于伴随制造业发展和货币工资支付而出现的地区性和地方银行。投资银行服务于不同的目的，提供一种新的货币创造形式。它们的出现既不是为了服务贸易，也不是为了服务工业，而是为了承销股份公司的创建并从中获利，主要是为修建铁路和其他基础设施，往往还是帝国规模的基础设施。它们管理公司债券和股票的发行，处理失败企业的重组，并安排合并和收购。与通常以合伙形式经营的较早银行不同，投资银行本身常常就是股份公司，出售从股票营销业务中获取的未来利润的索取权。
它们获得了惊人的货币创造权力。新的大型基础设施所许诺的未来收入的耐久性，以及帝国权力不断扩大的规模，使信用货币创造的装置得以大幅扩展。
en: As a machine for the intergenerational transfer of wealth, the joint-stock corporation needed the assistance of another organisation, investment banking. Investment banks differed from the older merchant banks, which financed colonial trade and chattel slavery and created the government debt required for the new scale of warfare on which those depended. They also differed from the provincial and local banks that accompanied the development of manufacturing and the payment of money wages. Investment banking served a different purpose, providing a new form of money creation. They emerged to serve neither trade nor industry, but to underwrite and profit from the creation of joint-stock companies, principally for the building of railways and other infrastructure, often on an imperial scale. They managed the issuing of corporate bonds and shares, handled the reorganisation of failed ventures, and arranged mergers and acquisitions. Unlike older banks, which were usually run as partnerships, they were frequently themselves joint-stock companies, selling claims on the future profits to be made from the business of marketing shares.

They acquired an astonishing power to create money. The durability of the future revenue promised by new, large-scale infrastructure and the growing scale of imperial power allowed a vastly expanded apparatus for the creation of credit money.

zh: 除了商业这一新领域，还出现了第二种构造这种扩大了的未来关系的机制：现代城市。从十九世纪后期起，大都市经历了一系列类似的技术变革，这些变革之所以可能，是因为用钢铁和混凝土建造，燃煤发电站的发展，电动安全电梯、电动有轨电车和电气轻轨的发明，以及利用法律安排和种族歧视来规划和管理空间的使用。
城市房地产开发商如今可以做与铁路企业家相同的事（他们常常就是同一批人）：竖起一座建筑，其价值从建成之日起就与建造成本关系不大。在靠碳燃料驱动的现代化城市里，房地产的价格对应于投机者出售未来几十年在该地块居住权的资本化价值。
en: Alongside the new sphere of business, there was a second object that emerged as a mechanism for constructing this expanded relationship to the future: the modern city. From the late nineteenth century, the metropolis was undergoing a similar set of technical changes, made possible by building with iron and steel and concrete, by the development of coal-fuelled electric power stations, by the invention of the electric safety elevator, the electric-powered tram, and electric light railways, and by employing legal arrangements along with race discrimination to plan and regulate the use of space.

Developers of urban property could now do the same thing as railway entrepreneurs (they were frequently the same persons): erect a structure whose value, from the day it was built, had little to do with the cost of its construction. The price of real estate, in the carbon-fuelled modernising city, corresponded to the capitalised value at which the speculator could sell the right to live for the next several decades on that spot of land.

zh: 大多数作家未能把城市理解为一种装置，一种像大型商业公司那样从未来攫取付款的装置。当政治经济学家和开发商不得不向人们解释，为什么住房价格可以远高于建造建筑的成本时，他们并没有从建筑物作为一种从未来抽取收入的机器所具有的扩大能力来解释这种差异；他们把在起作用的机制伪装起来，把剩余归因于自然不断变化的价值。他们说，城市开发把自然的或“未改良的”土地变成房地产。建造成本与建筑可售价格之间的差异，被归因于“土地”不断上涨的“价值”。1900 年，正如我们在导论中指出的，一位纽约建筑师把一座快速建成的商业建筑简单描述为“一台让土地付钱的机器”。
但付款并不来自土地，而来自空间未来的租户或购买者。土地只是托词。亨利·乔治和其他大多已被遗忘的政治经济学家等论者，曾反对用这种过于简单的方式，来解释投机者凭借房地产开发这一装置攫取未来收入的奇特能力。
然而，价格体系的新理论家把价值解释为一种产物，不是攫取装置的产物，而是一种被描绘为供求相互作用的简单机制的产物。这种耐久装置在技术上的新颖性很快就从视野中消失了，而价格机制在该装置中仅起次要作用。
en: Most writers failed to understand the city as an apparatus, like the large business corporation, for capturing payments from the future. When political economists and developers had to explain to people why the price of housing could become so much higher than the cost of erecting the building, they did not explain the difference in terms of the expanded ability of buildings to work as machines that extract revenue from the future; they disguised the mechanism at work by attributing the surplus to the changing value of nature. Urban development, they said, transformed natural or ‘unimproved’ land into real estate. The difference between the cost of construction and the price at which a building could be sold was ascribed to the rising ‘value’ of the ‘land’. In 1900, as we noted in the introduction, a New York architect described a rapidly built commercial building as simply ‘a machine that makes the land pay’.

But the payment came not from the land, but from the future renters or purchasers of the space. Land was merely the alibi. Writers like Henry George and other mostly forgotten political economists fought against this simplistic way of explaining the strange ability of speculators to capture future revenue through the device of property development.

However, the new theorists of the price system explained value as the product, not of an apparatus of capture, but of the simple mechanism pictured as an interaction of supply and demand. The technical novelty of the durable apparatus, in which the price mechanism played a minor part, soon disappeared from view.

zh: 人们可以把经济学家与一门新城市科学——城市规划领域——的创始人加以对比。苏格兰规划师和社会理论家帕特里克·格迪斯受到托斯丹·凡勃伦的影响，并像凡勃伦一样受到亨利·乔治的影响；他属于那些理解城市房地产非劳动价值如今代表的并非市场力量的作用、而是这种对未来、并因而对那些将通过住房成本上涨来偿还它的人之劳动的索取权的作家。格迪斯写道，现代城市“破败街道”和“破败房屋”中积累的财富，主要在于“对其他地区他人破败街道的文书索取权，以及对其
劳动的索取权”。
他和其他人提出的补救办法，是一种新实践——城市规划，用公民财富的创造和分配来平衡私人对未来劳动索取权的积累，尤其是通过建设花园城市——一种混合形式，用“城市与乡村生活健康、自然和经济的结合”取代工业城市的“破败街道”。
花园城市的先驱埃比尼泽·霍华德解释说，这种新型城乡形式的
目的，是通过收取全部地租并将其存入社区信托来获取房地产开发所创造的非劳动所得剩余。信托反过来支付公共工程、公园和其他设施的费用，并提供退休养老金以及事故和疾病保险。
在霍华德影响下，“红色维也纳”的规划师和建筑师——这座把公共住房作为两次世界大战之间欧洲城市生活社会民主愿景基础的城市——创造了共同攫取城市生活所创造价值的最戏剧性范例。
然而在实践中，这些优托邦式方案最容易在欧洲的海外殖民地推广，例如开罗周边赫利奥波利斯、马阿迪和花园城等街区的开发；把新德里建成殖民印度新首都；以及大雅法计划——巴勒斯坦城市雅法与其郊外不断扩张的犹太复国主义定居点特拉维夫组成的集合城市，由帕特里克·格迪斯本人绘制总体规划。
然而在大多数地方，规划者缺乏推行这种集体方案的权力；而殖民版本依靠种族排斥来管理空间使用，没有实施任何集体攫取和重新分配剩余的计划。由于建筑和产权具有新的耐久性和规模，城市生活成为另一种装置——与现代商业公司并列——企业家可以在其中把从后来者那里攫取的收入提前变现于当下。对空间的殖民化依赖于对时间的殖民化力量。
en: One can contrast the economists with the founders of a new science of the city, the field of urban planning. The Scottish planner and social theorist Patrick Geddes, influenced by Thorstein Veblen and, like Veblen, by Henry George, was among the writers who understood that the unearned value of urban property now represented not the working of market forces but this claim on the future, and thus on the labour of those who would repay it through the increased cost of their housing. The wealth accumulated in the ‘mean streets’ and ‘mean houses’ of the modern city, Geddes wrote, consists chiefly in ‘documentary claims upon other people’s mean streets elsewhere, and upon their labour

The remedy that he and others proposed was the new practice of town planning, to balance the accumulation of private claims upon future labour with the creation and distribution of civic wealth, in particular through the building of garden cities – a hybrid form in which the ‘mean streets’ of the industrial city would be replaced with ‘a healthy, natural, and economic combination of town and country life’.
The pioneer of the garden city, Ebenezer Howard, explained that the

purpose of this new urban-rural form was to capture the unearned surplus created by the development of property by collecting all ground rent and holding it in a community trust. The trust, in turn, would pay for public works, parks, and other amenities and for the provision of retirement pensions and insurance against accident and sickness.

Influenced by Howard, the planners and architects of Red Vienna, the city that made public housing the basis of a social democratic vision for urban life in interwar Europe, produced the most dramatic example of the shared capture of the value that urban living creates.

In practice, however, it was in Europe’s overseas colonies that these eutopic schemes were most easily promoted, with the development of districts such as Heliopolis, Maadi, and Garden City around Cairo; the building of New Delhi as a new capital for colonial India; and the plan for Greater Jaffa, the conurbation of the Palestinian city of Jaffa and the expanding Zionist settlement on its outskirts, Tel Aviv, for which Patrick Geddes himself drew up the master plan.

In most places, however, planners lacked the power to impose such collective schemes, while the colonial versions, relying on racial exclusion to manage the use of space, implemented none of the plans for the collective capture and redistribution of surplus. Thanks to the new durability and scale of buildings and property rights, urban living became another apparatus, alongside the modern business corporation, in which entrepreneurs could realise revenues in the present captured from those who would come later. The colonisation of space relied upon the powers of colonising time.

zh: 金融与实体
en: The Financial and the Real

zh: 让我们回到货币及其作为信用的制造这一问题，以及这种对货币的理解如何被遗忘。随着现代投资银行与现代商业公司和现代城市一同出现，那些论述新货币体系如何运作的人，可以毫无困难地说明货币是银行创造的东西。苏格兰政治经济学家亨利·邓宁·麦克劳德出版了最有影响的论述。
本章开篇提到的常驻开罗金融专家米切尔—英尼斯承认自己得益于麦克劳德的著作。麦克劳德写道，银行“不是‘借入’和‘贷出’货币的机构，而是一家信用的制造厂”。
en: Let us return to the question of money and its manufacture as credit, and how this understanding of money was forgotten. As modern investment banking emerged alongside the modern business corporation and the modern city, those who wrote about how the new monetary system worked had no problem in explaining that money was something created by banks. A Scottish political economist, Henry Dunning Macleod, published the most influential account.

Mitchell-Innes, the Cairo-based financial expert with whom this chapter began, acknowledged his debt to Macleod’s work. A bank, Macleod wrote, ‘is not an office for “borrowing” and “lending” money, but it is a Manufactory of credit’.

zh: 到二十世纪中叶，这种理解已在很大程度上消失。1960 年出版的一部经典著作

的作者们知道，大部分货币是由私人银行创造的。但他们把这视为一种残余现象。正如书名所示，他们的目的不是解释货币在银行中如何运作——他们没有研究实际的银行业务——而是说明如何让货币在“一种理论”中发挥作用。他们所说的理论，是指新古典经济学的假设。正统经济科学假定，所有经济现象都可以被理解为仿佛像价格机制那样组织起来：买卖双方交易商品和服务的安排。在这个理想化的世界里，贸易没有障碍。由于一种被称为“市场”的无摩擦金融平衡机制的运作，一种商品的供给总会自我调整到与需求相等。因此，货币是不需要的。在构成现代新古典经济学科学基础的经典阿罗—德布鲁模型中，货币并不存在。因此，货币和银行理论的目标不是弄清货币实际如何运作，而是在这个无摩擦的世界里为它安排一个人为的位置。
en: By the mid-twentieth century, this understanding had largely disappeared. The authors of a classic text published in 1960,

, were aware that most money was created by private banks. But they treated this as a residual phenomenon. As the book’s title indicated, their aim was not to explain how money works in banks – they made no study of actual banking – but how money can be made to work within ‘a theory’. By theory, they meant the assumptions of neoclassical economics. Orthodox economic science assumes that all economic phenomena can be understood as if they were organised as a price mechanism, an arrangement of buyers and sellers trading goods and services. In this idealised world there are no impediments to trade. The supply of a good always self-adjusts, thanks to the operations of a frictionless financial balancing mechanism called ‘the market’, to equal demand. As a result, there is no need for money. In the classic Arrow–Debreu model that formed the scientific basis of modern neoclassical economics, money does not exist. So, the goal of a theory of money and banking was not to find out how money actually worked. It was to make an artificial place for it in this frictionless world.

zh: 随着现代银行业的发展，私人创造信用货币的权力变得越来越不透明。日常实践掩盖了货币创造过程。人们变得对从未来攫取的方式浑然不觉。如果说工业化实现了“银行”与工厂的分离、以及“生产”时刻与信用供给的分离，那么公司、后来被称为“商业”的现象以及现代房地产的兴起，进一步加深了这种分离效果。
en: With the development of modern banking, the private power to create credit money became increasingly opaque. Everyday practices concealed the process of money creation. People became oblivious to the modes of extraction from the future. If industrialisation effected the separation of the ‘bank’ from the factory, and the moment of ‘production’ from the supply of credit, then the rise of the corporation, of the phenomenon that came to be called ‘business’, and of modern real estate, furthered this effect of separation.

zh: 与货币的本质一样，银行业的作用也一直被误解。在通俗看法中，银行是存放和贷出货币的地方，而不是制造货币的行业。银行似乎从客户那里吸收存款，然后把同样的资金贷给其他客户。正统经济理论采纳并强化了这种常识观点。
银行业提供一种教科书称之为“金融中介”的服务，把买者与卖者、借款人与储蓄者配对，并促进他们之间的互动。在这种观点中，银行可能还有进一步的作用，但只在银行彼此之间的关系中，即作为一种支付机制，执行国家的金融记账。
en: As with the nature of money, the role of banking has been misunderstood. In the popular view, a bank is a place that stores and lends out money, not an industry that manufactures it. Banks appear to take in deposits from their customers, then loan out those same funds to other customers. Orthodox economic theory adopts and reinforces this common-sense view.

Banking provides a service that textbooks describe as ‘financial intermediation’, aligning those who purchase with those who sell, and those who borrow with those who save, and facilitating their interaction. Banks may have a further role, in this view, but only in their relations with one another, operating as a payments mechanism that carries out the nation’s financial bookkeeping.

zh: 这种关于货币体系如何运作的通俗理解，被经济理论所复制，最近逐渐被认为在很大程度上是一种虚构。当银行向借款人提供资金时，它们并不是把吸收的存款贷出去。它们是在创造新货币。
制造过程如下。

一位个人客户或企业向银行申请贷款，比方说金额为 10 万美元。如果银行同意，它为借款人设立一个账户，并在账簿中记录该账户有这一数额的正余额。这笔钱并不是从其他资金——例如其他客户的储蓄——转移过来的。它是凭空创造的，仅仅通过记录一个 10 万美元的余额这一简单行为。银行可以无中生有地创造货币，因为这些资金虽然记入客户名下的账户，却从未离开银行。借款人不会提着一个装有现金的公文包走出银行（除非在极少数情况下，而且金额很小），也不会在结束网上交易时拿到现金。相反，借款人收到的是一份纸质对账单或电子记录，表明新资金可以使用。当客户决定花掉这些资金时，钱离开客户的账户——但仍留在银行体系的账簿中。例如，如果这笔钱作为购买房地产的首付花出去，银行会把资金记为从借款人账户中扣除，并贷记到出售房地产者的账户。如果卖方是同一家银行的客户，资金就留在该银行的账簿中。如果卖方使用不同的银行，两家机构就在银行之间的每日账目结算中，记录一笔从一家银行账簿到另一家银行账簿的转移。
en: This popular understanding of how the monetary system works, reproduced in economic theory, has recently come to be understood as largely a fiction. When banks make funds available to borrowers, they are not lending out the money they have taken in as deposits. They are creating new money.
The manufacturing works as follows.

An individual customer or firm requests a loan from the bank, say in the amount of $100,000. If the bank agrees, it sets up an account for the borrower and records in its books that the account has a positive balance of that amount. This money is not transferred from some other fund, such as the savings of other customers. It is created from scratch, by the simple act of recording a $100,000 balance. The bank can create money out of nothing because the funds, although credited to an account in the customer’s name, do not leave the bank. The borrower does not walk out of the bank’s premises, or terminate an online transaction, with actual cash in a briefcase (except in rare cases, and only in small amounts). Rather, the borrower receives a paper statement or an electronic record indicating the availability of the new funds. When the customer decides to spend the funds, the money leaves the customer’s account – but stays within the books of the banking system. If the money is spent as the deposit on the purchase of a property, for example, the bank marks the funds as debited from the account of the borrower, and credits them to the account of the person selling the property. If the seller is a customer of the same bank, the funds remain in the books of that bank. If the seller uses a different bank, the two institutions record a transfer from the ledger of one bank to the other, as part of the daily settlement of accounts between banks.

zh: 虽然上例中的银行创造了新的信用货币，但这些资金是通过相应的未来债务产生的。银行体系内创造的这些资金是对未来的索取权；其创造取决于对偿还这笔债务的未来付款的可靠支配。在接下来的数月或数年里，借款人将从未来收入中支付贷款金额，再加上银行收取的额外费用，作为使这笔未来债务付款今天可以由卖方即期获得的成本。这笔额外费用被称为贷款的“利息”。最好反过来看。未来债务将被全额偿还——其全部价值是本金加上“利息”。银行今天以折扣价把它提供给卖方——即未来向银行付款的贴现值。这个折扣（今天的较低价值）代表卖方为即期获得资金而支付的溢价。银行之所以能够今天即期提供未来资金，不是因为它向其他客户借入资金，而是因为它不断汇集其他客户的债务偿还。对未来债务的贴现正是货币的来源。
en: While the bank in this example has created new credit money, the funds have been brought into being through a corresponding future debt. The funds created within the banking system are a claim on the future; their creation depends on this reliable command of the future payment of the debt. Over the following months and years, the borrower will pay from future income the amount of the loan, plus the surplus charged by the bank as the cost of making that future debt payment available on demand to the seller today. This surcharge is described as the ‘interest’ on the loan. It is better to see it in reverse. The future debt will be repaid in full – its full value being the principal plus the ‘interest’. The bank makes it available to the seller today at a discount – the discounted present value of the future payment to the bank. The discount (the lower value today) represents a premium the seller pays in exchange for immediate access to the funds, on demand. The bank is able to offer the future funds on demand today, not because it takes in loans from other customers, but because it continuously pools the debt repayments of other customers. The discounting of future debts is the very source of money.

zh: 根据贷款期限和贴现率（被描绘为利率）以及任何相关费用，从未来收入中支付的金额可能达到所创造原始金额的两倍或更多。这样一来，银行体系对货币的创造本身就发挥着把未来收入转移到当下、并从这种对未来榨取中获利的作用。
en: Depending on the duration of the loan and the discount rate (portrayed as the rate of interest) along with any associated fees, the money paid from future income may amount to double the original sum created, or more. In this way, the very creation of money by the banking system operates to transfer future income to the present, and to profit from this extraction from the future.

zh: 随着现代银行业的出现，从未来攫取的方式不仅支配我们已经考察的具体领域——进行长途贸易、支付工资、建设基础设施、提供住房或创建股份公司。它支配着所有这些领域以及其他领域，而所有这些都使货币的制造成为一种使未来负债的方式。所有这一切反过来又取决于国家的作用；国家并不像通俗想象的那样是货币的来源，而是承认银行创造的信用为货币的机构，特别是通过接受它以缴纳税款。
en: With modern banking, the mode of extraction from the future comes to govern not only the specific fields we have already considered – the conduct of long-distance trade, the payment of wages, the building of infrastructure, the provision of housing, or the creation of joint-stock companies. It governs all these and more, all of which enable the manufacture of money as a mode of indebting the future. All of them depend, in turn, on the role of the state, which operates not as the source of money, as is popularly imagined, but as the agency that recognises bank-created credit as money, in particular via its acceptance of this for the payment of taxes.

zh: 我们现在可以理解，为什么我们通常看不到货币如何运作。这里有三个问题。第一，可以称之为国家效应：只有极少量货币——估计约为 3%——采取硬币和纸币这种现成、可见的形式。这一小部分有形货币由公共造币厂或货币机构发行，并印有权威标志。我们把这个可见对象误认为整体，并假定所有货币都源自政府，通过公共手段生产。第二，日常经验效应：当个人或企业确实遇到银行创造货币的权力时——例如借款购买一辆车或一处房产，或取得公司贷款——他们得到一个自己名下的账户，列明新增资金。由于这如今是客户的钱，它似乎不再属于银行。然而，正如我们现在所知，尽管账户上写着客户的名字，这笔钱从未离开银行。
en: We can now understand why we do not normally see how money works. There are three issues. First, what one could call the state effect: only a very small amount of money, estimated at around 3 per cent, takes the ready, visible form of coins and banknotes. That small, tangible part is issued by a public mint or monetary agency and printed with symbols of authority. We mistake this visible object for the whole and assume that all money originates in government and is produced through public means. Second, the effect of everyday experience: when individuals or firms do encounter the power of banks to create money – for example, when borrowing funds to purchase, say, a vehicle or a property, or when taking out a company loan – they are given an account in their own name listing the new funds. Since this is now the customer’s money, it seems no longer to belong to the bank. Yet, as we now know, despite the name on the account, that money never leaves the bank.

zh: 第三，也是最重要的，是我们不妨称之为经济效应的东西。正如我们将在
中看到、并在最后一章进一步探讨的，在二十世纪，把经济建构为政治和科学对象，只给金融留下一个次要位置。经济是一种衡量和描绘真实商品与服务流动的方式，以价格为代表。这种流动主要发生在两个部门之间，即企业和家庭，它们被表现为整体的互补部分。企业生产商品和服务，而家庭在同一时间点购买这些
商品和服务，以其劳动作为交换。货币只被认为是促进这种即时交换的手段，而不是一种组织起来从这一过程和其他过程的时间运作中攫取剩余的信用装置。经济理论反映了这种简单的安排。经济在促成物质与货币、实体与表象、商业与银行之间表面上的分离方面的这一作用，是接下来各章要探讨的特征。
en: Third, and most important, there is what we might call the economy effect. As we will see in

and explore further in the final chapter, in the twentieth century, the construction of the economy as an object of politics and science allowed only a secondary place for finance. The economy was a way of measuring and picturing the movement of real goods and services, represented by prices. This movement happened largely between two sectors, business firms and households, represented as complementary parts of a whole. Firms produced goods and services, while households in the same temporal moment purchased those goods

and services in exchange for their labour. Money was considered only a means of facilitating this instantaneous exchange, not as an apparatus of credit organised to extract a surplus from the temporal operation of this and other processes. Economic theory reflected this simple arrangement. This role of the economy in effecting the apparent separation of the material and the monetary, the real and the represented, the business and the bank, is a feature to be explored in the coming chapters.

zh: 我们如今全神贯注于我们与未来的关系，却在很大程度上对其最日常的机制浑然不觉。货币，我们以为只是一种便利的简单物品，或一种记录实际事物价值的表象体系，结果却是一种从未来抽取收入的无所不在的机制。然而，它无法独自做到这一点。
en: We are preoccupied today with our relationship to the future, but largely oblivious of its most everyday mechanism. Money, which we think of as just a simple object of convenience or a system of representation for recording the values of actual things, turns out to be a ubiquitous mechanism for the extraction of future income. However, it cannot do this alone.

zh: 大多数关于我们与未来关系的论述都是倒着写的。问题不仅在于时间顺序的颠倒，还在于解释与被解释现象之间的颠倒。习惯做法是从一种简单的唯物主义出发，把生活视为一系列需要满足的未来需求。为了满足这些需求，必须生产和分配商品。生产需要土地、设备、能源供应和分配基础设施。这些又需要信用供给，信用还可以为原料供应和成品购买提供资金。简单的唯物主义始于一个简单的未来，即由这样一种决定所召唤的未来：从必须满足的预期需求出发开始解释。这些需求把未来与当下连接起来。信用供给被描绘成对一系列似乎源于物质生活条件之要求的回应。在这种本末倒置的叙述中，信用随后才出现，作为一种补充。它为当下提供了一条回到那个未来的路径。
en: Most accounts of our relationship to the future are written backwards. The problem is a reversal not just of the temporal sequence, but of the explanation and the phenomenon to be explained. The habit is to begin from a simple materialism, where life is thought of as a set of future needs to be met. To satisfy those needs, goods must be produced and distributed. Their production requires land, equipment, the supply of energy, and an infrastructure of distribution. These, in turn, require the provision of credit, which can also finance the supply of raw materials and the purchase of finished goods. Simple materialism starts in a simple future, the future conjured by the decision to begin the explanation from the standpoint of prospective needs that must be satisfied. Those needs connect the future back to the present. The supply of credit is portrayed as a response to a set of requirements that appear to arise from the material conditions of life. Credit comes afterwards, in this back-to-front account, as a supplement. It supplies the present with a path back to that future.

zh: 我们现在已经颠倒了这一顺序，避开了它简单的唯物主义。我们已经知道，随着大规模商业关系的扩展，信用并不是为服务贸易需要而创造的次要事物。恰恰相反，贸易是为了服务于信用创造而被组织起来的。同样，银行业也不只是一个“中介”，通过匹配借款人的需求与贷方可提供的资金来服务家庭和企业的需要。它变成了一家“制造厂”，一座制造信用货币的大型工场。
en: We have now reversed this sequence, avoiding its simple materialism. We already know that, with the spread of large-scale commercial relations, credit was not something secondary, created to serve the needs of trade. If anything, trade was organised to serve the creation of credit. Likewise, banking was not just an ‘intermediary’ that served the needs of households and businesses, by matching the demands of borrowers to the availability of lenders. It became a ‘Manufactory’, a large workshop for the manufacturing of credit money.

zh: 这种颠倒并不要求我们放弃对物质过程的分析，转而研究金融的非物质形式。它要求一种不同的唯物主义：在这种唯物主义中，金融不是
实体的对立面；相反，这种对立的生产——金融似乎与实体分离——本身就是一种需要研究和解释的效果。它还要求一种不同的未来观：不把未来视为由物质需求投射所召唤的想象世界，而视为为了从后来者那里、以牺牲共同未来为代价，占有财富和生计而建造的具体装置。
en: This reversal does not require us to abandon the analysis of material processes in favour of studying the immaterial forms of finance. It requires a different materialism, one in which the financial is not the

opposite of the real, but, rather, one in which the production of this opposition, in which finance appears to stand apart from the real, is an effect to be studied and explained. And it requires a different approach to the future, seeing it not as the imaginary world conjured by the projection of material needs, but as the concrete apparatus built for the appropriation of wealth and livelihoods from those who come later, and at the expense of the common future.
